title.zh: 卷6 帝紀第6 武帝下
title.raw: 卷6 帝紀第6 武帝下 Volume 6 Annals 6: Emperor Wu 2

sentences.zh: 武帝下

translations.literal: Emperor Wu, Part Two.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu, Part Two.

sentences.zh: 建德四年春正月戊辰，以柱國枹罕公辛威為寧州總管，太原公王康為襄州總管。

translations.literal: First month of spring in the fourth year of Jiande, day wuchen, Pillar-of-State Duke of Baohan Xin Wei was made governor-general of Ning Province, and Duke of Taiyuan Wang Kang was made governor-general of Xiang Province.
translations.idiomatic: First month of spring in the fourth year of Jiande (575), on wuchen day, Pillar-of-State Xin Wei, Duke of Baohan, was made governor-general of Ning Province, and Wang Kang, Duke of Taiyuan, was made governor-general of Xiang Province.

sentences.zh: 初置營軍器監。

translations.literal: For the first time the Directorate of Military Equipment was established.
translations.idiomatic: The Directorate of Military Equipment was established for the first time.

sentences.zh: 壬申，詔曰：「今陽和布氣，品物資始，敬授民時，義兼敦勸。

translations.literal: On renshen day an edict said: "Now yang harmony spreads its breath; all things receive their beginning. Respectfully granting the people's seasons carries the meaning of earnest encouragement as well.
translations.idiomatic: On renshen day an edict declared: "Now warm harmony spreads abroad and all things begin anew. Granting the seasons to the people is also a call to earnest encouragement.

sentences.zh: 《詩》不云乎：『弗躬弗親，庶民弗信。

translations.literal: Does the Book of Poetry not say: 'If one does not personally attend and personally oversee, the common people will not trust.
translations.idiomatic: Does the Book of Poetry not say: 'Unless the ruler himself attends and oversees, the common people will not trust him.

sentences.zh: 』刺史守令，宜親勸農，百司分番，躬自率導。

translations.literal: ' Provincial inspectors and prefects should personally encourage agriculture; the hundred offices in rotation should themselves lead and guide.
translations.idiomatic: ' Provincial inspectors and prefects should personally encourage farming; the hundred offices, taking turns, should lead by example.

sentences.zh: 事非機要，並停至秋。

translations.literal: Affairs not urgent should all be suspended until autumn.
translations.idiomatic: Non-urgent business should all be suspended until autumn.

sentences.zh: 鰥寡孤獨不能自存者，所在量加賑恤。

translations.literal: Widowers, widows, orphans, and the childless unable to support themselves should wherever necessary receive added relief.
translations.idiomatic: Widowers, widows, orphans, and the solitary who cannot support themselves should receive added relief wherever needed.

sentences.zh: 逋租懸調，兵役殘功，並宜蠲免。

translations.literal: Delinquent rent, suspended levies, and unfinished military or corvée labor should all be remitted.
translations.idiomatic: Overdue rent, suspended levies, and unfinished military service or corvée should all be remitted.

sentences.zh: 」癸酉，行幸同州。

translations.literal: " On guiyou day he traveled to Tong Province.
translations.idiomatic: " On guiyou day he traveled to Tong Province.

sentences.zh: 二月丙戌朔，日有蝕之。

translations.literal: Second month, first day bingxu, there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: Second month, on the first day, bingxu, there was a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 辛卯，改置宿衛官員。

translations.literal: On xinmao day the palace guard offices were reorganized.
translations.idiomatic: On xinmao day the palace guard offices were reorganized.

sentences.zh: 己酉，柱國、廣德公李意有罪免。

translations.literal: On jiyou day Pillar-of-State Li Yi, Duke of Guangde, was removed from office for crime.
translations.idiomatic: On jiyou day Pillar-of-State Li Yi, Duke of Guangde, was dismissed for crime.

sentences.zh: 三月丙辰，遣小司寇淮南西元

translations.literal: Third month, on bingchen day, Minor Director of Governance Huainan Xiyuan
translations.idiomatic: Third month, on bingchen day, Minor Director of Governance Huainan Xiyuan

translations.literal: (Wei)
translations.idiomatic: (Wei)

sentences.zh: 〔偉〕、納言伊婁謙使於齊。

translations.literal: [Wei] and Speaking Minister Yilou Qian were sent as envoys to Northern Qi.
translations.idiomatic: [Wei] and Speaking Minister Yilou Qian were sent as envoys to Northern Qi.

sentences.zh: 郡縣各省主簿一人。

translations.literal: Each commandery and county was to have one chief clerk.
translations.idiomatic: Each commandery and county was reduced to one chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 丙寅，至自同州。

translations.literal: On bingyin day he returned from Tong Province.
translations.idiomatic: On bingyin day he returned from Tong Province.

sentences.zh: 甲戌，以柱國、趙王招為雍州牧。

translations.literal: On jiaxu day Pillar-of-State Prince of Zhao Zhao was made governor of Yong Province.
translations.idiomatic: On jiaxu day Pillar-of-State Prince of Zhao Zhao was made governor of Yong Province.

sentences.zh: 夏四月甲午，柱國、燕國公于寔有罪免。

translations.literal: Summer, fourth month, on jiawu day, Pillar-of-State Yu Shi, Duke of Yan, was removed from office for crime.
translations.idiomatic: Summer, fourth month, on jiawu day, Pillar-of-State Yu Shi, Duke of Yan, was dismissed for crime.

sentences.zh: 丁酉，初令上書者並為表，于皇太子以下稱啟。

translations.literal: On dingyou day it was first ordered that memorialists should all submit memorial tables, and that below the crown prince the form "petition" should be used.
translations.idiomatic: On dingyou day it was first ordered that all memorials be submitted as formal tables, and that below the crown prince the term "petition" be used.

sentences.zh: 六月，詔東南道四總管內，自去年以來新附之戶，給復三年。

translations.literal: Sixth month, an edict said that within the four governor-generals of the Southeast Circuit, newly submitted households since last year should receive three years' tax and corvée exemption.
translations.idiomatic: Sixth month, an edict granted three years' tax and corvée exemption to newly submitted households within the four Southeast Circuit governor-generals since the previous year.

sentences.zh: 秋七月丙辰，行幸雲陽宮。

translations.literal: Autumn, seventh month, on bingchen day, he traveled to the Yunyang Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Autumn, seventh month, on bingchen day, he traveled to the Yunyang Palace.

sentences.zh: 己未，禁五行大布錢不得出入關，布泉錢聽入而不聽出。

translations.literal: On jiwei day the Five-Element Great Cloth coin was prohibited from passing through the passes; Cloth-Quan coin was permitted to enter but not to leave.
translations.idiomatic: On jiwei day the Five-Element Great Cloth coin was barred from crossing the passes; Cloth-Quan coin could enter but not leave.

sentences.zh: 丁卯，至自雲陽宮。

translations.literal: On dingmao day he returned from the Yunyang Palace.
translations.idiomatic: On dingmao day he returned from the Yunyang Palace.

sentences.zh: 甲戌，陳遣使來聘。

translations.literal: On jiaxu day Chen sent envoys on a friendly visit.
translations.idiomatic: On jiaxu day Chen sent envoys on a friendly visit.

sentences.zh: 丙子，召大將軍以上于大德殿，帝曰：「太祖神武膺運，創造王基，兵威所臨，有征無戰。

translations.literal: On bingzi day he summoned all generals and above to the Hall of Great Virtue. The emperor said: "Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai, divinely martial, received the mandate and founded the royal foundation; wherever military might reached, there was campaign without battle.
translations.idiomatic: On bingzi day he summoned all generals and above to the Hall of Great Virtue. Emperor Wu said: "Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai, divinely martial, received Heaven's mandate and laid the royal foundation; wherever his armies went, he campaigned without needing battle.

sentences.zh: 唯彼偽齊，猶懷跋扈。

translations.literal: Only that false Northern Qi still harbored insolence.
translations.idiomatic: Only the false Northern Qi still nursed defiance.

sentences.zh: 雖復戎車屢駕，而大勳未集。

translations.literal: Though war-chariots were repeatedly dispatched, the great achievement was not yet gathered.
translations.idiomatic: Though war-chariots were sent out again and again, the great victory was not yet won.

sentences.zh: 朕以寡昧，纂承鴻緒，往以政出權宰，無所措懷。

translations.literal: I, being dull and ignorant, succeeded to the great undertaking; formerly because government issued from the power-holding minister, I had nowhere to put my heart.
translations.idiomatic: I, being dull and ignorant, succeeded to the great mandate; formerly, with government in the hands of the power-holding minister, I had no room to act.

sentences.zh: 自親覽萬機，便圖東討。

translations.literal: Since I have personally handled the myriad tasks, I have plotted the eastern punitive campaign.
translations.idiomatic: Since I have personally taken charge of affairs, I have planned an eastern punitive campaign.

sentences.zh: 惡衣菲食，繕甲治兵，數年已來，戰備稍足。

translations.literal: Wearing poor clothes and eating frugal food, repairing armor and training troops—for several years now the war preparations have gradually become sufficient.
translations.idiomatic: Wearing plain clothes and eating sparingly, repairing armor and drilling troops—for several years now our war preparations have gradually become adequate.

sentences.zh: 而偽主昏虐，恣行無道，伐暴除亂，斯實其時。

translations.literal: Yet their false ruler is benighted and cruel, wantonly practicing wrongdoing; to strike down the violent and remove chaos—this is truly the time.
translations.idiomatic: Yet their false ruler is benighted and cruel and acts without restraint; to punish the violent and end the chaos—now is truly the time.

sentences.zh: 今欲數道出兵，水陸兼進，北拒太行之路，東扼黎陽之險。

translations.literal: Now I wish to send troops on several routes, advancing by land and water together, blocking the road of the Taihang to the north and seizing the peril of Liyang to the east.
translations.idiomatic: Now I intend to send troops on several routes by land and water together, blocking the Taihang road to the north and holding the strategic point of Liyang to the east.

sentences.zh: 若攻拔河陰，兗、豫則馳檄可定。

translations.literal: If we capture Heyin, Yan and Yu can be settled by dispatching proclamations.
translations.idiomatic: If we take Heyin, Yan and Yu can be secured by dispatching proclamations alone.

sentences.zh: 然後養銳享士，以待其至。

translations.literal: Then nurturing sharpness and feasting the soldiers, we await their arrival.
translations.idiomatic: Then, resting the troops and keeping them keen, we await the enemy's advance.

sentences.zh: 但得一戰，則破之必矣。

translations.literal: With just one battle, crushing them is certain.
translations.idiomatic: One battle will surely break them.

sentences.zh: 王公以為何如？

translations.literal: What do you lords think?
translations.idiomatic: What do you lords think?

sentences.zh: 」羣臣咸稱善。

translations.literal: " All the ministers praised it as good.
translations.idiomatic: " All the ministers approved.

sentences.zh: 丁丑，詔曰：

translations.literal: On dingchou day an edict said:
translations.idiomatic: On dingchou day an edict declared:

sentences.zh: 高氏因時放命，據有汾、漳，擅假名器，歷年永久。

translations.literal: The Gao clan seized the moment and threw off restraint, holding Fen and Zhang, usurping titles and regalia for many years.
translations.idiomatic: The Gao clan seized the moment and cast off all restraint, holding the Fen and Zhang regions and usurping titles and regalia for many years.

sentences.zh: 朕以亭毒為心，遵養時晦，遂敦聘好，務息黎元。

translations.literal: I have taken nurturing all things as my heart, followed the way of biding my time in obscurity, and so cultivated friendly embassies, striving to give the people rest.
translations.idiomatic: I have taken nurturing the realm as my heart, bided my time in obscurity, and cultivated friendly embassies, striving to give the people peace.

sentences.zh: 而彼懷惡不悛，尋事侵軼，背言負信，竊邑藏奸。

translations.literal: Yet they harbored evil without reform, soon launched encroachments and raids, betrayed their words and violated faith, and harbored traitors while seizing territory.
translations.idiomatic: Yet they harbored malice without reform, soon launched raids and encroachments, broke their word and betrayed trust, and seized territory while hiding traitors.

sentences.zh: 往者軍下宜陽，釁由彼始；

translations.literal: Formerly when our army descended on Yiyang, the provocation began from them;
translations.idiomatic: When our army descended on Yiyang in the past, the provocation came from them;

sentences.zh: 兵興汾曲，事非我先。

translations.literal: when arms arose at Fen Bend, the initiative was not mine.
translations.idiomatic: when arms were raised at Fen Bend, the initiative was not mine.

sentences.zh: 此獲俘囚，禮送相繼；

translations.literal: We captured prisoners and respectfully sent them back in succession;
translations.idiomatic: We captured prisoners and respectfully returned them one after another;

sentences.zh: 彼所拘執，曾無一反。

translations.literal: those they held, not one was ever returned.
translations.idiomatic: those they held captive, not one was ever returned.

sentences.zh: 加以淫刑妄逞，毒賦繁興，齊、魯軫殄悴之哀，幽、并啟來蘇之望。

translations.literal: Added to this were wanton cruel punishments and oppressive taxes repeatedly imposed; Qi and Lu echoed the grief of extermination and exhaustion; You and Bing awakened hopes of returning to life.
translations.idiomatic: To this were added wanton punishments and crushing levies; Qi and Lu echoed the grief of ruin and exhaustion, and You and Bing awakened hopes of deliverance.

sentences.zh: 旣禍盈惡稔，衆叛親離，不有一戎，何以大定。

translations.literal: Since misfortune is full and evil ripe, the masses rebel and kin depart—without one armed campaign, how can there be great settlement?
translations.idiomatic: Since their evil is ripe and their doom full, the people rebel and kin turn away—without one campaign, how can the realm be settled?

sentences.zh: 今白藏在辰，涼風戒節，厲兵詰暴，時事惟宜。

translations.literal: Now the white dew is stored in the season; cool winds warn of the season's change. Sharpening arms and punishing the violent—the time alone is fitting.
translations.idiomatic: Now white dew marks the season and cool winds warn of its turn. To sharpen arms and punish the violent—no time is more fitting.

sentences.zh: 朕當親禦六師，龔行天罰。

translations.literal: I shall personally lead the Six Armies and act in accord with Heaven's punishment.
translations.idiomatic: I shall personally lead the Six Armies and execute Heaven's punishment.

sentences.zh: 庶憑祖宗之靈，潛資將士之力，風馳九有，電掃八紘。

translations.literal: May we rely on the spirits of the ancestral temple and secretly draw on the strength of officers and soldiers, sweeping the nine domains like the wind and scouring the eight directions like lightning.
translations.idiomatic: May we rely on the ancestral spirits and the strength of our officers and soldiers, sweeping the nine domains like the wind and scouring the eight directions like lightning.

sentences.zh: 可分命衆軍，指期進發。

translations.literal: Let the various armies be assigned and ordered to advance on the appointed day.
translations.idiomatic: Let the various armies be assigned and ordered to advance on the appointed day.

sentences.zh: 以柱國陳王純為前一軍總管，滎陽公司馬消難為前二軍總管，鄭國公達奚震為前三軍總管，越王盛為後一軍總管，周昌公侯莫陳瓊為後二軍總管，趙王招為後三軍總管，齊王憲率衆二萬趣黎陽，隨國公楊堅、廣甯侯薛回舟師三萬自渭入河，柱國梁國公侯莫陳芮率衆一萬守太行道，申國公李穆帥衆三萬守河陽道，常山公于翼帥衆二萬出陳、汝。

translations.literal: Pillar-of-State Prince of Chen Chun was made commander of the first forward army; Duke of Xingyang Sima Xiaonan was made commander of the second forward army; Duke of Zheng Daxi Zhen was made commander of the third forward army; Prince of Yue Sheng was made commander of the first rear army; Duke of Zhouchang Houmochen Qiong was made commander of the second rear army; Prince of Zhao Zhao was made commander of the third rear army; Prince of Qi Xian led twenty thousand troops toward Liyang; Duke of Sui Yang Jian and Marquis of Guangning Xue Hui with thirty thousand naval troops entered the Yellow River from the Wei; Pillar-of-State Houmochen Rui, Duke of Liang, led ten thousand men to hold the Taihang route; Duke of Shen Li Mu commanded thirty thousand to hold the Heyang route; Duke of Changshan Yu Yi commanded twenty thousand to advance from Chen and Ru.
translations.idiomatic: Pillar-of-State Prince of Chen Chun was made commander of the first forward army; Sima Xiaonan, Duke of Xingyang, of the second forward army; Daxi Zhen, Duke of Zheng, of the third forward army; Prince of Yue Sheng of the first rear army; Houmochen Qiong, Duke of Zhouchang, of the second rear army; Prince of Zhao Zhao of the third rear army; Prince of Qi Xian led twenty thousand men toward Liyang; Yang Jian, Duke of Sui, and Xue Hui, Marquis of Guangning, with thirty thousand naval troops entered the Yellow River from the Wei; Pillar-of-State Houmochen Rui, Duke of Liang, led ten thousand to hold the Taihang route; Li Mu, Duke of Shen, commanded thirty thousand to hold the Heyang route; Yu Yi, Duke of Changshan, commanded twenty thousand to advance from Chen and Ru.

sentences.zh: 壬午，上親率六軍，衆六萬，直指河陰。

translations.literal: On renwu day the emperor personally led the Six Armies, sixty thousand strong, straight toward Heyin.
translations.idiomatic: On renwu day Emperor Wu personally led the Six Armies, sixty thousand strong, straight toward Heyin.

sentences.zh: 八月癸卯，入于齊境。

translations.literal: Eighth month, on guimao day, he entered Northern Qi territory.
translations.idiomatic: Eighth month, on guimao day, he entered Northern Qi territory.

sentences.zh: 禁伐樹踐苗稼，犯者以軍法從事。

translations.literal: Cutting trees and trampling crops was forbidden; violators were dealt with by military law.
translations.idiomatic: Cutting trees and trampling crops was forbidden; violators were punished under military law.

sentences.zh: 丁未，上親率諸軍攻河陰大城，拔之。

translations.literal: On dingwei day the emperor personally led the various armies in attacking the great city of Heyin and captured it.
translations.idiomatic: On dingwei day Emperor Wu personally led the armies in attacking the great city of Heyin and took it.

sentences.zh: 進攻子城，未克。

translations.literal: They pressed the attack on the inner city but did not capture it.
translations.idiomatic: They pressed the attack on the inner city but failed to take it.

sentences.zh: 上有疾。

translations.literal: The emperor fell ill.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu fell ill.

sentences.zh: 九月辛酉夜，班師，水軍焚舟而退。

translations.literal: Ninth month, on xinyou night, the army withdrew; the naval force burned its boats and retreated.
translations.idiomatic: Ninth month, on xinyou night, the army withdrew; the naval force burned its boats and retreated.

sentences.zh: 齊王憲及于翼、李穆等所在克捷，降拔三十餘城，皆棄而不守。

translations.literal: Prince of Qi Xian and Yu Yi, Li Mu, and others wherever they went achieved victory; more than thirty cities were captured or surrendered, and all were abandoned without being held.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Qi Xian, Yu Yi, Li Mu, and others won victories wherever they went; more than thirty cities were taken or surrendered, but all were abandoned without being garrisoned.

sentences.zh: 唯以王藥城要害，令儀同三司韓正守之。

translations.literal: Only Wangyao city, a strategic point, was left for Third Rank Opening-the-Feudatory Equal-to-the-Three-Divisions Han Zheng to hold.
translations.idiomatic: Only Wangyao city, a strategic point, was left for Han Zheng, opening-the-feudatory of third rank equal to the Three Divisions, to hold.

sentences.zh: 正尋以城降齊。

translations.literal: Before long Zheng surrendered the city to Northern Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Zheng surrendered the city to Northern Qi.

sentences.zh: 戊寅，至自東伐。

translations.literal: On wuyin day he returned from the eastern campaign.
translations.idiomatic: On wuyin day he returned from the eastern campaign.

sentences.zh: 己卯，以華州刺史、畢王賢為荊州總管。

translations.literal: On jimao day Hua Province inspector Prince of Bi Xian was made governor-general of Jing Province.
translations.idiomatic: On jimao day Prince of Bi Xian, inspector of Hua Province, was made governor-general of Jing Province.

sentences.zh: 冬十月戊子，初置上柱國、上大將軍官，改開府儀同三司為開府儀同大將軍，儀同三司為儀同大將軍，又置上開府、上儀同官。

translations.literal: Tenth month of winter, on wuzi day, the offices of supreme pillar-of-state and supreme grand general were established for the first time; Opening-the-Feudatory Equal-to-the-Three-Divisions was changed to Opening-the-Feudatory Equal Grand General, Third Rank Equal-to-the-Three-Divisions to Third Rank Equal Grand General, and the offices of supreme opening-the-feudatory and supreme equal rank were also established.
translations.idiomatic: Tenth month of winter, on wuzi day, the offices of supreme pillar-of-state and supreme grand general were established; Opening-the-Feudatory Equal-to-the-Three-Divisions was renamed Opening-the-Feudatory Equal Grand General, Third Rank Equal-to-the-Three-Divisions became Third Rank Equal Grand General, and the offices of supreme opening-the-feudatory and supreme equal rank were also created.

sentences.zh: 甲午，行幸同州。

translations.literal: On jiawu day he traveled to Tong Province.
translations.idiomatic: On jiawu day he traveled to Tong Province.

sentences.zh: 閏月，齊將尉相貴寇大寧，延州總管王慶擊走之。

translations.literal: Intercalary month, Northern Qi general Wei Xianggui raided Daning; Yan Province governor-general Wang Qing drove him off.
translations.idiomatic: Intercalary month, Northern Qi general Wei Xianggui raided Daning; Yan Province governor-general Wang Qing drove him off.

sentences.zh: 以柱國齊王憲、蜀國公尉遲迥為上柱國，柱國代王達為益州總管，大司寇滎陽公司馬消難為梁州總管。

translations.literal: Pillar-of-State Prince of Qi Xian and Duke of Shu Yuchi Jiong were made supreme pillars-of-state; Pillar-of-State Prince of Dai Da was made governor-general of Yi Province; Grand Director of Governance Sima Xiaonan, Duke of Xingyang, was made governor-general of Liang Province.
translations.idiomatic: Pillar-of-State Prince of Qi Xian and Yuchi Jiong, Duke of Shu, were made supreme pillars-of-state; Pillar-of-State Prince of Dai Da was made governor-general of Yi Province; Sima Xiaonan, Duke of Xingyang and grand director of governance, was made governor-general of Liang Province.

sentences.zh: 詔諸畿郡各舉賢良。

translations.literal: An edict ordered each metropolitan commandery to recommend worthy men.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered each metropolitan commandery to recommend worthy men.

sentences.zh: 十一月己亥，改置司內官員。

translations.literal: Eleventh month, on jihai day, the offices within the Directorate of the Inner Court were reorganized.
translations.idiomatic: Eleventh month, on jihai day, the offices of the Directorate of the Inner Court were reorganized.

sentences.zh: 十二月辛亥朔，日有食之。

translations.literal: Twelfth month, first day xinhai, there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: Twelfth month, on the first day, xinhai, there was a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 庚午，至自同州。

translations.literal: On gengwu day he returned from Tong Province.
translations.idiomatic: On gengwu day he returned from Tong Province.

sentences.zh: 丙子，陳遣使來聘。

translations.literal: On bingzi day Chen sent envoys on a friendly visit.
translations.idiomatic: On bingzi day Chen sent envoys on a friendly visit.

sentences.zh: 是歲，岐、寧二州民饑，開倉賑給。

translations.literal: That year the people of Qi and Ning provinces suffered famine; granaries were opened for relief.
translations.idiomatic: That year the people of Qi and Ning provinces suffered famine; granaries were opened for relief.

sentences.zh: 五年春正月癸未，行幸同州。

translations.literal: First month of spring in the fifth year, on guiwei day, he traveled to Tong Province.
translations.idiomatic: First month of spring in the fifth year, on guiwei day, he traveled to Tong Province.

sentences.zh: 辛卯，行幸河東涑川，集關中、河東諸軍校獵。

translations.literal: On xinmao day he traveled to Hedong and the Su River, gathering the military officers of Guanzhong and Hedong for a hunt.
translations.idiomatic: On xinmao day he traveled to Hedong and the Su River and gathered the officers of Guanzhong and Hedong for a hunt.

sentences.zh: 甲午，還同州。

translations.literal: On jiawu day he returned to Tong Province.
translations.idiomatic: On jiawu day he returned to Tong Province.

sentences.zh: 丁酉，詔曰：「朕克己思治，而風化未弘。

translations.literal: On dingyou day an edict said: "I restrain myself and think on good governance, yet customs and teaching are not yet broad.
translations.idiomatic: On dingyou day an edict declared: "I restrain myself and strive for good governance, yet customs and teaching are not yet widespread.

sentences.zh: 永言前古，載懷夕惕。

translations.literal: Speaking always of antiquity, I carry evening vigilance in my heart.
translations.idiomatic: Reflecting always on antiquity, I keep vigilance in my heart.

sentences.zh: 可分遣大使，周省四方，察訟聽謠，問民恤隱。

translations.literal: Let grand envoys be dispatched in all directions to tour and inspect the four quarters, examine lawsuits, listen to songs, and inquire into the people's hidden distress.
translations.idiomatic: Let grand envoys be dispatched in all directions to tour the realm, examine lawsuits, listen to popular songs, and inquire into the people's hidden distress.

sentences.zh: 其獄犴無章，侵漁黎庶，隨事究驗，條錄以聞。

translations.literal: Where prisons are lawless and officials plunder the common people, let each case be investigated on the spot and a record submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Where prisons are lawless and officials plunder the people, let each case be investigated on the spot and reported.

sentences.zh: 若政績有施，治綱克舉；

translations.literal: Where achievements in governance have been applied and the governing framework well maintained;
translations.idiomatic: Where achievements in governance have been shown and the governing framework well maintained;

sentences.zh: 及行宣圭蓽，道著丘園：並須撿審，依名騰奏。

translations.literal: and where one has practiced the way while dwelling in humble thatch, making virtue known from the hills and gardens: all should be examined and reported by name.
translations.idiomatic: and where one has practiced the way in humble thatch and made virtue known from seclusion: all should be examined and reported by name.

sentences.zh: 其鰥寡孤獨，寔可哀矜，亦宜賑給，務使周贍。

translations.literal: As for widowers, widows, orphans, and the solitary who truly deserve pity, relief should also be given so that they are fully provided for.
translations.idiomatic: Widowers, widows, orphans, and the solitary who truly deserve pity should also receive relief so that they are fully provided for.

sentences.zh: 」廢布泉錢。

translations.literal: " Cloth-Quan coin was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: " Cloth-Quan coin was abolished.

sentences.zh: 戊申，初令鑄錢者絞，其從者遠配為民。

translations.literal: On wushen day it was first ordered that coin counterfeiters be strangled and their accomplices banished far away as commoners.
translations.idiomatic: On wushen day it was first ordered that coin counterfeiters be strangled and their accomplices banished far away as commoners.

sentences.zh: 二月辛酉，遣皇太子贇巡撫西土，仍討吐谷渾，戎事節度，並宜隨機專決。

translations.literal: Second month, on xinyou day, Crown Prince Yun was sent to tour and pacify the western lands and also to campaign against Tuyuhun; military dispositions might all be decided on the spot as circumstances required.
translations.idiomatic: Second month, on xinyou day, Crown Prince Yun was sent to tour and pacify the western lands and also to campaign against Tuyuhun; he was authorized to decide military dispositions on the spot as circumstances required.

sentences.zh: 三月庚子，月犯東井第一星。

translations.literal: Third month, on gengzi day, the moon encroached upon the first star of the Well.
translations.idiomatic: Third month, on gengzi day, the moon encroached upon the first star of the Well.

sentences.zh: 壬寅，至自同州。

translations.literal: On renyin day he returned from Tong Province.
translations.idiomatic: On renyin day he returned from Tong Province.

sentences.zh: 文宣皇后服再期，戊申，祥。

translations.literal: When the second mourning period for Empress Wenxuan ended, on wushen day the end-of-mourning rites were performed.
translations.idiomatic: When the second mourning period for Empress Wenxuan ended, on wushen day the end-of-mourning rites were performed.

sentences.zh: 夏四月乙卯，行幸同州。

translations.literal: Summer, fourth month, on yimao day, he traveled to Tong Province.
translations.idiomatic: Summer, fourth month, on yimao day, he traveled to Tong Province.

sentences.zh: 開府、清河公宇文神舉攻拔齊陸渾等五城。

translations.literal: Opening-the-Feudatory Yuwen Shenju, Duke of Qinghe, captured five Northern Qi cities including Luhun.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Shenju, Duke of Qinghe and opening-the-feudatory, captured five Northern Qi cities including Luhun.

sentences.zh: 五月壬辰，至自同州。

translations.literal: Fifth month, on renchen day, he returned from Tong Province.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth month, on renchen day, he returned from Tong Province.

sentences.zh: 六月戊申朔，日有食之。

translations.literal: Sixth month, first day wushen, there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: Sixth month, on the first day, wushen, there was a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，祠太廟。

translations.literal: On xinhai day sacrifice was offered at the Imperial Ancestors' Temple.
translations.idiomatic: On xinhai day he sacrificed at the Imperial Ancestors' Temple.

sentences.zh: 丙辰，利州總管、紀王康有罪，賜死。

translations.literal: On bingchen day Li Province governor-general Prince of Ji Kang was guilty of crime and was granted death.
translations.idiomatic: On bingchen day Prince of Ji Kang, governor-general of Li Province, was guilty of crime and was put to death by imperial order.

sentences.zh: 丁巳，行幸雲陽宮。

translations.literal: On dingsi day he traveled to the Yunyang Palace.
translations.idiomatic: On dingsi day he traveled to the Yunyang Palace.

sentences.zh: 月掩心後星。

translations.literal: The moon masked the star behind the Heart.
translations.idiomatic: The moon masked the star behind the Heart.

sentences.zh: 庚午，熒惑入輿鬼。

translations.literal: On gengwu day Mars entered Ghost Carriage.
translations.idiomatic: On gengwu day Mars entered Ghost Carriage.

sentences.zh: 秋七月乙未，京師旱。

translations.literal: Autumn, seventh month, on yiwei day, the capital suffered drought.
translations.idiomatic: Autumn, seventh month, on yiwei day, the capital suffered drought.

sentences.zh: 八月戊申，皇太子伐吐谷渾，至伏俟城而還。

translations.literal: Eighth month, on wushen day, the crown prince campaigned against Tuyuhun, reached Fuyu city, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Eighth month, on wushen day, the crown prince campaigned against Tuyuhun, reached Fuyu city, and returned.

sentences.zh: 乙卯，至自雲陽宮。

translations.literal: On yimao day he returned from the Yunyang Palace.
translations.idiomatic: On yimao day he returned from the Yunyang Palace.

sentences.zh: 乙丑，陳遣使來聘。

translations.literal: On yichou day Chen sent envoys on a friendly visit.
translations.idiomatic: On yichou day Chen sent envoys on a friendly visit.

sentences.zh: 九月丁丑，大醮於正武殿，以祈東伐。

translations.literal: Ninth month, on dingchou day, a great Daoist rite was held at the Hall of Correct Martialness to pray for the eastern campaign.
translations.idiomatic: Ninth month, on dingchou day, a great Daoist rite was held at the Hall of Correct Martialness to pray for success in the eastern campaign.

sentences.zh: 冬十月，帝謂羣臣曰：「朕去歲屬有疹疾，遂不得克平逋寇。

translations.literal: Tenth month of winter, the emperor said to the assembled ministers: "Last year I happened to suffer illness and so could not completely subdue the lingering enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Tenth month of winter, Emperor Wu said to the assembled ministers: "Last year I happened to fall ill and so could not completely subdue the lingering enemy.

sentences.zh: 前入賊境，備見敵情，觀彼行師，殆同兒戲。

translations.literal: On my previous entry into enemy territory I saw their situation at first hand; watching them take the field, it was nearly child's play.
translations.idiomatic: On my previous entry into enemy territory I saw their situation at first hand; watching them take the field, it was nearly child's play.

sentences.zh: 又聞其朝政昏亂，政由羣小，百姓嗷然，朝不謀夕。

translations.literal: I also hear that their court government is benighted and chaotic, policy rests with petty men, the people cry out in distress, and they do not plan beyond the morning for the evening.
translations.idiomatic: I also hear that their court is benighted and chaotic, policy rests with petty men, the people cry out in distress, and they do not plan beyond the morning for the evening.

sentences.zh: 天與不取，恐貽後悔。

translations.literal: If Heaven's gift is not taken, I fear regret will follow.
translations.idiomatic: If Heaven's gift is not taken, I fear we shall regret it afterward.

sentences.zh: 若復同往年，出軍河外，直為撫背，未扼其喉。

translations.literal: If we again do as in former years and send the army beyond the river, we would merely pat their back and not seize their throat.
translations.idiomatic: If we again do as in former years and send the army beyond the river, we would merely pat their back and not seize their throat.

sentences.zh: 然晉州本高歡所起之地，鎮攝要重，今往攻之，彼必來援，吾嚴軍以待，擊之必克。

translations.literal: Yet Jin Province is the very land from which Gao Huan rose; its garrison holds a vital position. If we attack it now, they are sure to come to its aid; we shall hold our army ready and await them, and in striking them we are certain to prevail.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Jin Province is the very land from which Gao Huan rose and holds a vital position. If we attack it now, they will surely come to its aid; we shall hold our army ready and await them, and in striking them we are certain to prevail.

sentences.zh: 然後乘破竹之勢，鼓行而東，足以窮其窟穴，混同文軌。

translations.literal: Then, riding the momentum of splitting bamboo, we can advance east with drums beating, enough to exhaust their lair and unite writing and wheel-tracks.
translations.idiomatic: Then, riding the momentum of splitting bamboo, we can advance east with drums beating, enough to overrun their lair and unite the realm under one rule.

sentences.zh: 」諸將多不願行。

translations.literal: Most of the generals were unwilling to go.
translations.idiomatic: Most of the generals were unwilling to go.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「幾者事之微，不可失矣。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "The subtle point of affairs must not be lost.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu said: "The subtle point of affairs must not be lost.

sentences.zh: 若有沮吾軍者，朕當以軍法裁之。」

translations.literal: Whoever discourages my army, I shall punish by military law."
translations.idiomatic: Whoever discourages my army, I shall punish by military law."

sentences.zh: 己酉，帝總戎東伐。

translations.literal: On jiyou day the emperor took overall command of the eastern campaign.
translations.idiomatic: On jiyou day Emperor Wu took overall command of the eastern campaign.

sentences.zh: 以越王盛為右一軍總管，杞國公亮為右二軍總管，隨國公楊堅為右三軍總管，譙王儉為左一軍總管，大將軍竇

translations.literal: Prince of Yue Sheng was made commander of the first right army; Duke of Qi Liang was made commander of the second right army; Duke of Sui Yang Jian was made commander of the third right army; Prince of Qiao Jian was made commander of the first left army; Grand General Dou
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Yue Sheng was made commander of the first right army; Liang, Duke of Qi, of the second right army; Yang Jian, Duke of Sui, of the third right army; Prince of Qiao Jian of the first left army; Grand General Dou

translations.literal: (Tai)
translations.idiomatic: (Tai)

sentences.zh: 〔恭〕為左二軍總管，廣化公丘崇為左三軍總管，齊王憲、陳王純為前軍。

translations.literal: [Gong] was made commander of the second left army; Duke of Guanghua Qiu Chong was made commander of the third left army; Prince of Qi Xian and Prince of Chen Chun were the forward army.
translations.idiomatic: [Gong] was made commander of the second left army; Qiu Chong, Duke of Guanghua, of the third left army; Prince of Qi Xian and Prince of Chen Chun led the forward army.

sentences.zh: 庚戌，熒惑犯太微上將。

translations.literal: On gengxu day Mars encroached upon the supreme general of the Supreme Palace.
translations.idiomatic: On gengxu day Mars encroached upon the supreme general of the Supreme Palace.

sentences.zh: 戊午，歲星犯太陵。

translations.literal: On wuwu day Jupiter encroached upon the Great Mound.
translations.idiomatic: On wuwu day Jupiter encroached upon the Great Mound.

sentences.zh: 癸亥，帝至晉州，遣齊王憲率精騎二萬守雀鼠谷，陳王純步騎二萬守千里徑，鄭國公達奚震步騎一萬守統軍川，大將軍韓明步騎五千守齊子嶺，

translations.literal: On guihai day the emperor reached Jin Province and dispatched Prince of Qi Xian to lead twenty thousand elite cavalry to hold Sparrow-Rat Pass, Prince of Chen Chun with twenty thousand infantry and cavalry to hold Thousand-Li Path, Duke of Zheng Daxi Zhen with ten thousand infantry and cavalry to hold Commanding-Generals River, Grand General Han Ming with five thousand infantry and cavalry to hold Qizi Ridge,
translations.idiomatic: On guihai day Emperor Wu reached Jin Province and dispatched Prince of Qi Xian with twenty thousand elite cavalry to hold Sparrow-Rat Pass, Prince of Chen Chun with twenty thousand infantry and cavalry to hold Thousand-Li Path, Daxi Zhen, Duke of Zheng, with ten thousand infantry and cavalry to hold Commanding-Generals River, Grand General Han Ming with five thousand infantry and cavalry to hold Qizi Ridge,

translations.literal: (Yan)
translations.idiomatic: (Yan)

sentences.zh: 〔烏〕氏公尹昇步騎五千守

translations.literal: [Wu] Clan Duke Yin Sheng with five thousand infantry and cavalry held
translations.idiomatic: [Wu] Clan Duke Yin Sheng with five thousand infantry and cavalry held

translations.literal: (Zhong)
translations.idiomatic: (Zhong)

sentences.zh: 鼓〔鐘〕鎮，涼城公辛韶步騎五千守蒲津關，柱國、趙王招步騎一萬自華谷攻齊汾州諸城，柱國宇文盛步騎一萬守汾水關。

translations.literal: Drum [Zhong] Fort; Duke of Liangcheng Xin Shao with five thousand infantry and cavalry held Pujin Pass; Pillar-of-State Prince of Zhao Zhao with ten thousand infantry and cavalry attacked Northern Qi's Fen Province cities from Huagu; Pillar-of-State Yuwen Sheng with ten thousand infantry and cavalry held Fen River Pass.
translations.idiomatic: Drum [Zhong] Fort; Xin Shao, Duke of Liangcheng, with five thousand infantry and cavalry held Pujin Pass; Pillar-of-State Prince of Zhao Zhao with ten thousand infantry and cavalry attacked Northern Qi's Fen Province cities from Huagu; Pillar-of-State Yuwen Sheng with ten thousand infantry and cavalry held Fen River Pass.

sentences.zh: 遣內史王誼監六軍，攻晉州城。

translations.literal: Director of the Palace Secretariat Wang Yi was sent to supervise the Six Armies in attacking Jin Province city.
translations.idiomatic: Director of the Palace Secretariat Wang Yi was sent to supervise the Six Armies in attacking Jin Province city.

sentences.zh: 帝屯于汾曲。

translations.literal: The emperor encamped at Fen Bend.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu encamped at Fen Bend.

sentences.zh: 齊王憲攻洪洞、永安二城，並拔之。

translations.literal: Prince of Qi Xian attacked the two cities of Hongdong and Yongan and captured both.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Qi Xian attacked Hongdong and Yongan and captured both.

sentences.zh: 是夜，虹見於晉州城上，首向南，尾入紫微宮，長十餘丈。

translations.literal: That night a rainbow appeared above Jin Province city, its head pointing south and its tail entering the Purple Palace, more than ten zhang long.
translations.idiomatic: That night a rainbow appeared above Jin Province city, its head pointing south and its tail entering the Purple Palace, more than ten zhang long.

sentences.zh: 帝每日自汾曲赴城下，親督戰，城中惶窘。

translations.literal: Each day the emperor came from Fen Bend to below the city wall and personally directed the fighting; inside the city panic and distress mounted.
translations.idiomatic: Each day Emperor Wu came from Fen Bend to below the walls and personally directed the fighting; inside the city panic mounted.

sentences.zh: 庚午，齊行臺左丞侯子欽出降。

translations.literal: On gengwu day Northern Qi's mobile headquarters left aide Hou Ziqin came out and surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: On gengwu day Hou Ziqin, left aide of Northern Qi's mobile headquarters, came out and surrendered.

sentences.zh: 壬申，齊晉州刺史崔景嵩守城北面，夜密遣使送款，上開府王軌率衆應之。

translations.literal: On renshen day Northern Qi Jin Province inspector Cui Jingsong held the city's north face; by night he secretly sent envoys to offer submission, and Opening-the-Feudatory Wang Gui led troops to respond.
translations.idiomatic: On renshen day Cui Jingsong, Northern Qi inspector of Jin Province, held the city's north face; by night he secretly sent envoys to offer submission, and Wang Gui, opening-the-feudatory, led troops to respond.

sentences.zh: 未明，登城鼓噪，齊衆潰，遂克晉州，擒其城主特進、開府、海昌王尉相貴，俘甲士八千人，送關中。

translations.literal: Before dawn they mounted the wall and raised a clamor; the Northern Qi forces collapsed, and Jin Province was taken. Its city commander, special grandee, opening-the-feudatory, Prince of Haichang Wei Xianggui, was captured; eight thousand armored soldiers were taken prisoner and sent to Guanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Before dawn they mounted the walls and raised a clamor; the Northern Qi forces collapsed and Jin Province was taken. Its commander Wei Xianggui, special grandee, opening-the-feudatory, and Prince of Haichang, was captured; eight thousand armored soldiers were taken prisoner and sent to Guanzhong.

sentences.zh: 甲戌，以上開府梁士彥為晉州刺史，加授大將軍，留精兵一萬以鎮之。

translations.literal: On jiaxu day Opening-the-Feudatory Liang Shiyan was made Jin Province inspector and additionally appointed grand general; ten thousand elite troops were left to garrison it.
translations.idiomatic: On jiaxu day Liang Shiyan, opening-the-feudatory, was made inspector of Jin Province and additionally appointed grand general; ten thousand elite troops were left to garrison it.

sentences.zh: 又遣諸軍徇齊諸城鎮，並相次降款。

translations.literal: The various armies were also sent to overrun Northern Qi cities and fortresses; all in succession offered submission.
translations.idiomatic: Other armies were also sent to overrun Northern Qi cities and fortresses; all in succession offered submission.

sentences.zh: 十一月己卯，齊主自幷州率衆來援。

translations.literal: Eleventh month, on jimao day, the Northern Qi ruler personally led troops from Bing Province to relieve the city.
translations.idiomatic: Eleventh month, on jimao day, the Northern Qi ruler personally led troops from Bing Province to relieve the city.

sentences.zh: 帝以其兵新集，且避之，乃詔諸軍班師，遣齊王憲為後拒。

translations.literal: The emperor, considering that their army was newly gathered, wished to avoid them and so ordered the various armies to withdraw; Prince of Qi Xian was dispatched as rear guard.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu, considering that the enemy army was newly gathered, wished to avoid battle and ordered the armies to withdraw; Prince of Qi Xian was dispatched as rear guard.

sentences.zh: 是日，齊主至晉州，憲不與戰，引軍度汾。

translations.literal: That day the Northern Qi ruler reached Jin Province; Xian did not give battle and led his army across the Fen.
translations.idiomatic: That day the Northern Qi ruler reached Jin Province; Xian did not give battle and led his army across the Fen.

sentences.zh: 齊主遂圍晉州，晝夜攻之。

translations.literal: The Northern Qi ruler then besieged Jin Province, attacking day and night.
translations.idiomatic: The Northern Qi ruler then besieged Jin Province, attacking day and night.

sentences.zh: 齊王憲屯諸軍于涑水，為晉州聲援。

translations.literal: Prince of Qi Xian encamped the various armies at the Su River as a supporting force for Jin Province.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Qi Xian encamped the armies at the Su River to support Jin Province.

sentences.zh: 河東地震。

translations.literal: Hedong suffered an earthquake.
translations.idiomatic: Hedong suffered an earthquake.

sentences.zh: 癸巳，至自東伐。

translations.literal: On guisi day he returned from the eastern campaign.
translations.idiomatic: On guisi day he returned from the eastern campaign.

sentences.zh: 獻俘於太廟。

translations.literal: Captives were presented at the Imperial Ancestors' Temple.
translations.idiomatic: Captives were presented at the Imperial Ancestors' Temple.

sentences.zh: 甲午，詔曰：「偽齊違信背約，惡稔禍盈，是以親總六師，問罪汾、晉。

translations.literal: On jiawu day an edict said: "The false Northern Qi violated faith and broke treaty; evil is ripe and misfortune full. Therefore I personally led the Six Armies to demand account at Fen and Jin.
translations.idiomatic: On jiawu day an edict declared: "The false Northern Qi violated faith and broke treaty; their evil is ripe and their doom full. Therefore I personally led the Six Armies to demand account at Fen and Jin.

sentences.zh: 兵威所及，莫不摧殄，賊衆危惶，烏棲自固。

translations.literal: Wherever military might reached, none was not destroyed; the enemy masses were fearful and alarmed, clinging like crows roosting in their nests.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever our armies reached, none escaped destruction; the enemy masses were fearful and alarmed, clinging to their nests like roosting crows.

sentences.zh: 暨元戎反旆，方來聚結，遊魂境首，尚敢趑趄。

translations.literal: When the main army turned its banners and withdrew, they had just begun to gather again; these wandering souls at the border still dared to hesitate and falter.
translations.idiomatic: When the main army turned its banners and withdrew, they had just begun to gather again; these wandering souls at the border still dared to hesitate and falter.

sentences.zh: 朕今更率諸軍，應機除剪。

translations.literal: I now lead the various armies again to cut them down as circumstances require."
translations.idiomatic: I now lead the armies again to cut them down as circumstances require."

sentences.zh: 」丙申，放齊諸城鎮降人還。

translations.literal: On bingshen day Northern Qi captives from the various cities and fortresses that had surrendered were released and sent home.
translations.idiomatic: On bingshen day Northern Qi captives from the surrendered cities and fortresses were released and sent home.

sentences.zh: 丁酉，帝發京師。

translations.literal: On dingyou day the emperor departed the capital.
translations.idiomatic: On dingyou day Emperor Wu departed the capital.

sentences.zh: 壬寅，度河，與諸軍合。

translations.literal: On renyin day he crossed the river and joined the various armies.
translations.idiomatic: On renyin day he crossed the river and joined the armies.

sentences.zh: 十二月戊申，次於晉州。

translations.literal: Twelfth month, on wushen day, he halted at Jin Province.
translations.idiomatic: Twelfth month, on wushen day, he halted at Jin Province.

sentences.zh: 初，齊攻晉州，恐王師卒至，于城南穿塹，自喬山屬於汾水。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Northern Qi attacked Jin Province, fearing that the imperial army might arrive suddenly, they dug a moat south of the city from Qiao Mountain to the Fen River.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Northern Qi attacked Jin Province, fearing a sudden arrival of the imperial army, they dug a moat south of the city from Qiao Mountain to the Fen River.

sentences.zh: 庚戌，帝帥諸軍八萬人，置陣東西二十餘里。

translations.literal: On gengxu day the emperor led eighty thousand men of the various armies and drew up battle lines more than twenty li from east to west.
translations.idiomatic: On gengxu day Emperor Wu led eighty thousand men and drew up battle lines more than twenty li from east to west.

sentences.zh: 帝乘常御馬，從數人巡陣處分，所至輒呼主帥姓名以慰勉之。

translations.literal: The emperor rode his usual horse with only a few men, touring the lines and giving dispositions; wherever he went he called out the commanders' names to comfort and encourage them.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu rode his usual horse with only a few men, touring the lines and giving orders; wherever he went he called out commanders by name to comfort and encourage them.

sentences.zh: 將士感見知之恩，各思自厲。

translations.literal: The officers and soldiers, moved by the grace of being known, each thought to exert himself.
translations.idiomatic: Officers and soldiers, moved by being personally recognized, each resolved to exert himself.

sentences.zh: 將戰，有司請換馬。

translations.literal: As battle was about to begin, the relevant offices requested that he change horses.
translations.idiomatic: As battle was about to begin, the relevant offices requested that he change horses.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「朕獨乘良馬何所之？

translations.literal: The emperor said: "If I alone ride a fine horse, where would I go?"
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu said: "If I alone ride a fine horse, where would I go?"

sentences.zh: 」齊主亦於塹北列陣。

translations.literal: The Northern Qi ruler also drew up battle lines north of the moat.
translations.idiomatic: The Northern Qi ruler also drew up battle lines north of the moat.

sentences.zh: 申後，齊人填塹南引。

translations.literal: After the shen hour the Northern Qi men filled the moat and advanced south.
translations.idiomatic: After the shen hour the Northern Qi forces filled the moat and advanced south.

sentences.zh: 帝大喜，勒諸軍擊之，齊人便退。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly pleased and ordered the various armies to strike; the Northern Qi men at once withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu was greatly pleased and ordered the armies to strike; the Northern Qi forces at once withdrew.

sentences.zh: 齊主與其麾下數十騎走還幷州。

translations.literal: The Northern Qi ruler with several dozen horsemen of his retinue fled back to Bing Province.
translations.idiomatic: The Northern Qi ruler fled back to Bing Province with several dozen horsemen of his retinue.

sentences.zh: 齊衆大潰，軍資甲仗，數百里間，委棄山積。

translations.literal: The Northern Qi masses collapsed in great rout; military stores, armor, and weapons were abandoned in heaps for hundreds of li.
translations.idiomatic: The Northern Qi masses collapsed in great rout; military stores, armor, and weapons lay abandoned in heaps for hundreds of li.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，帝幸晉州，仍率諸軍追齊主。

translations.literal: On xinhai day the emperor visited Jin Province and still led the various armies in pursuit of the Northern Qi ruler.
translations.idiomatic: On xinhai day Emperor Wu visited Jin Province and still led the armies in pursuit of the Northern Qi ruler.

sentences.zh: 諸將固請還師，帝曰：「縱敵患生。

translations.literal: The generals firmly requested withdrawal; the emperor said: "To let the enemy go breeds disaster.
translations.idiomatic: The generals firmly requested withdrawal; Emperor Wu said: "To let the enemy go breeds disaster.

sentences.zh: 卿等若疑，朕將獨往。

translations.literal: If you are doubtful, I shall go alone."
translations.idiomatic: If you are doubtful, I shall go alone."

sentences.zh: 」諸將不敢言。

translations.literal: The generals did not dare speak further.
translations.idiomatic: The generals did not dare speak further.

sentences.zh: 甲寅，齊主遣其丞相高阿那肱守高壁。

translations.literal: On jiayin day the Northern Qi ruler sent his chief minister Gao Anagou to hold Gaobi.
translations.idiomatic: On jiayin day the Northern Qi ruler sent his chief minister Gao Anagou to hold Gaobi.

sentences.zh: 帝麾軍直進，那肱望風退散。

translations.literal: The emperor waved his army straight forward; Anagou fled at the sight of the wind.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu drove his army straight forward; Anagou fled at the first sight of it.

sentences.zh: 丙辰，師次介休，齊將韓建業舉城降，以為上柱國，封郇國公。

translations.literal: On bingchen day the great army halted at Jiexiu; Northern Qi general Han Jianye surrendered the city and was made supreme pillar-of-state and enfeoffed as Duke of Xun.
translations.idiomatic: On bingchen day the great army halted at Jiexiu; Northern Qi general Han Jianye surrendered the city and was made supreme pillar-of-state and enfeoffed as Duke of Xun.

sentences.zh: 丁巳，大軍次幷州，齊主留其從兄安德王延宗守幷州，自將輕騎走鄴。

translations.literal: On dingsi day the great army halted at Bing Province; the Northern Qi ruler left his cousin Prince of Ande Yan Zong to hold Bing Province and himself led light cavalry to flee to Ye.
translations.idiomatic: On dingsi day the great army halted at Bing Province; the Northern Qi ruler left his cousin Prince of Ande Yan Zong to hold Bing Province and himself fled to Ye with light cavalry.

sentences.zh: 是日，詔〔齊王公以下〕曰：

translations.literal: That day an edict [to Northern Qi's kings, dukes, and below] said:
translations.idiomatic: That day an edict [to Northern Qi's kings, dukes, and below] declared:

sentences.zh: 〔夫樹之以君，司牧黔首，蓋以除其苛慝，恤其患害。

translations.literal: [To install rulers to govern the black-haired people is to remove their harsh oppression and relieve their distress.
translations.idiomatic: [To install rulers to govern the people is to remove their harsh oppression and relieve their distress.

sentences.zh: 朕君臨萬國，志清四海，思濟一世之人，寘之仁壽之域。

translations.literal: I rule the myriad states, my aim to pacify the four seas, thinking to succor the people of this age and place them in the domain of benevolence and long life.
translations.idiomatic: I rule the myriad states, my aim to pacify the four seas, thinking to succor the people of this age and place them in the domain of benevolence and long life.

sentences.zh: 嗟彼齊趙，獨為匪民，乃睠東顧，載深長想。

translations.literal: Alas for Qi and Zhao—they alone are lawless people; therefore I turn my gaze eastward, carrying deep and long concern.
translations.idiomatic: Alas for Qi and Zhao—they alone are lawless people; therefore I turn my gaze eastward with deep and long concern.

sentences.zh: 偽主涼德早聞，醜聲夙著，酒色是耽，盤遊是悅。

translations.literal: Their false ruler's cold virtue has long been heard of; his ugly reputation was noted early. He indulges in wine and women and delights in roaming and play.
translations.idiomatic: Their false ruler's cold virtue has long been known; his ugly reputation was noted early. He indulges in wine and women and delights in roaming and play.

sentences.zh: 閹豎居阿衡之任，胡〕人寄喉唇之重。

translations.literal: Eunuchs hold the office of prime counselor; Hu] people hold positions of vital trust.
translations.idiomatic: Eunuchs hold the office of prime counselor; non-Han people hold positions of vital trust.

sentences.zh: 棟樑骨鯁，翦為仇讐；

translations.literal: Pillars and beams, the hard bones of state, are cut down into enemies;
translations.idiomatic: Pillars and beams, the hard bones of state, are cut down into enemies;

sentences.zh: 狐、趙緒餘，降成皁隸。

translations.literal: the remnant threads of the Hu and Zhao clans are reduced to menial slaves.
translations.idiomatic: the remnant threads of the Hu and Zhao clans are reduced to menial slaves.

sentences.zh: 民不見德，唯虐是聞。

translations.literal: The people see no virtue—only cruelty is heard of.
translations.idiomatic: The people see no virtue—only cruelty is heard of.

sentences.zh: 朕懷茲漏網，置之度外，正欲各靜封疆，共紓民瘼故也。

translations.literal: I harbored these escaped from the net and set them outside my reckoning, wishing only that each should keep his own borders quiet and together relieve the people's afflictions.
translations.idiomatic: I harbored these escaped from the net and set them outside my reckoning, wishing only that each should keep his own borders quiet and together relieve the people's afflictions.

sentences.zh: 爾之主相，曾不是思，欲構厲階，反貽其梗。

translations.literal: Yet your ruler and chief minister never thought on this; they wished to build a ladder of trouble and instead brought calamity upon themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Yet your ruler and chief minister never thought on this; they wished to build a ladder of trouble and instead brought calamity upon themselves.

sentences.zh: 我之率土，咸求倳刃，帷幄獻兼弱之謀，爪牙奮干戈之勇，贏糧坐甲，若赴私讐。

translations.literal: Throughout my realm all seek to bare their blades; within the tent counsels of attacking the weak are offered, and among my claws and teeth the brave flourish with weapons—winning provisions and sitting in armor as if rushing to private vengeance.
translations.idiomatic: Throughout my realm all seek to bare their blades; within the tent counsels of attacking the weak are offered, and among my warriors the brave flourish with weapons—gathering provisions and sitting in armor as if rushing to private vengeance.

sentences.zh: 是以一鼓而定晉州，再舉而摧逋醜。

translations.literal: Therefore one drumbeat settled Jin Province; a second blow shattered the lingering foe.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore one drumbeat settled Jin Province; a second blow shattered the lingering foe.

sentences.zh: 偽丞相高阿那肱驅逼餘燼，竊據高壁；

translations.literal: The false chief minister Gao Anagou drove the remaining embers and secretly held Gaobi;
translations.idiomatic: The false chief minister Gao Anagou drove the remaining embers and secretly held Gaobi;

sentences.zh: 偽定南王韓建業作守介休，規相抗擬。

translations.literal: the false Prince of Dingnan Han Jianye held Jiexiu and plotted mutual resistance.
translations.idiomatic: the false Prince of Dingnan Han Jianye held Jiexiu and plotted mutual resistance.

sentences.zh: 聊示兵威，應時崩潰，那肱則單馬宵遁，建業則面縛軍和，爾之逃卒，所知見也。

translations.literal: We showed military might only briefly and they collapsed at once: Anagou fled alone by night on a single horse, and Jianye bound himself and surrendered at the army's approach—as your fugitive soldiers have themselves seen.
translations.idiomatic: We showed military might only briefly and they collapsed at once: Anagou fled alone by night on a single horse, and Jianye bound himself and surrendered at the army's approach—as your fugitive soldiers have themselves seen.

sentences.zh: 若其懷遠以德，則爾難以德綏；

translations.literal: If one treats distant peoples with virtue, you would be hard to pacify by virtue;
translations.idiomatic: If one treats distant peoples with virtue, you would be hard to pacify by virtue;

sentences.zh: 處鄰以義，則爾難以義服。

translations.literal: if one treats neighbors with righteousness, you would be hard to subdue by righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: if one treats neighbors with righteousness, you would be hard to subdue by righteousness.

sentences.zh: 且天與不取，道家所忌，攻昧侮亡，兵之上術。

translations.literal: Moreover, not taking Heaven's gift is what the Daoists warn against; attacking the benighted and despising the perishing is the highest art of war.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, not taking Heaven's gift is what the Daoists warn against; attacking the benighted and despising the perishing is the highest art of war.

sentences.zh: 朕今親馭羣雄，長驅宇內，六軍舒旆，萬隊啟行。

translations.literal: I now personally lead the assembled heroes, driving far within the realm; the Six Armies unfurl their banners and ten thousand columns set out.
translations.idiomatic: I now personally lead the assembled heroes, driving far within the realm; the Six Armies unfurl their banners and ten thousand columns set out.

sentences.zh: 勢與雷電爭威，氣逐風雲齊舉。

translations.literal: Our momentum vies with thunder and lightning in might; our spirit rises with wind and cloud together.
translations.idiomatic: Our momentum vies with thunder and lightning in might; our spirit rises with wind and cloud together.

sentences.zh: 王師所次，已達近郊，望歲之民，室家相慶，來蘇之後，思副厥誠。

translations.literal: Where the royal army halts has already reached the near suburbs; the people who await the harvest celebrate in their homes, and after returning to life they wish to match this sincerity.
translations.idiomatic: Where the royal army halts has already reached the near suburbs; the people who await deliverance celebrate in their homes, and after returning to life they wish to match this sincerity.

sentences.zh: 偽主若妙盡人謀，深達天命，牽羊道左，銜璧轅門，當惠以焚櫬之恩，待以列侯之禮。

translations.literal: If their false ruler exhausts human counsel and deeply comprehends Heaven's mandate, leading a sheep by the road's left and holding a jade disc at the chariot yoke, he shall be treated with the grace of burning the bales and received with the courtesy due a marquis.
translations.idiomatic: If their false ruler exhausts human counsel and deeply comprehends Heaven's mandate, leading a sheep by the road's left and holding a jade disc at the chariot yoke, he shall be treated with the grace of burning the bales and received with the courtesy due a marquis.

sentences.zh: 偽將相王公已下，衣冠士民之族，如有深識事宜，建功立效，官榮爵賞，各有加隆。

translations.literal: False generals, ministers, kings, and dukes and below, and the families of gentry and common people—if any deeply understand affairs and establish achievement and merit, office, glory, rank, and reward shall each be increased and elevated.
translations.idiomatic: False generals, ministers, kings, and dukes and below, and the families of gentry and common people—if any deeply understand affairs and establish achievement and merit, office, glory, rank, and reward shall each be increased and elevated.

sentences.zh: 若下愚不移，守迷莫改，則委之執憲，以正刑書。

translations.literal: If the lower stupid do not change and cling to error without reform, then they shall be handed to the law officers to be judged by the penal code.
translations.idiomatic: If the lower stupid do not change and cling to error without reform, then they shall be handed to the law officers to be judged by the penal code.

sentences.zh: 嗟爾庶士，胡寧自棄。

translations.literal: Alas, you common people—how can you abandon yourselves?
translations.idiomatic: Alas, you common people—how can you abandon yourselves?

sentences.zh: 或我之將卒，逃彼逆朝，無問貴賤，皆從蕩滌。

translations.literal: Or if my officers and soldiers have fled to that rebellious court, regardless of noble or base, all shall be swept away.
translations.idiomatic: Or if my officers and soldiers have fled to that rebellious court, regardless of noble or base, all shall be swept away.

sentences.zh: 善求多福，無貽後悔。

translations.literal: Seek good fortune diligently and do not leave regret behind.
translations.idiomatic: Seek good fortune diligently and do not leave regret behind.

sentences.zh: 璽書所至，咸使聞知。

translations.literal: Wherever the imperial seal-edicts reached, all were made to hear and know.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever the imperial edicts reached, all were notified.

sentences.zh: 自是齊之將帥，降者相繼。

translations.literal: From this time onward, Qi generals and commanders surrendered in succession.
translations.idiomatic: From then on Northern Qi generals surrendered one after another.

sentences.zh: 封其特進、開府賀拔伏恩為郜國公，其餘官爵各有差。

translations.literal: Its specially advanced, opening-the-feudatory Helba Fu'en was enfeoffed as Duke of Gao state; the rest received offices and ranks each according to difference.
translations.idiomatic: Helba Fu'en, specially advanced and opening-the-feudatory, was enfeoffed as Duke of Gao; the others received offices and ranks as appropriate.

sentences.zh: 戊午，高延宗僭卽偽位，改年德昌。

translations.literal: On wuwu day Gao Yanzong presumptuously took the false throne and changed the era name to Dechang.
translations.idiomatic: On wuwu day Gao Yanzong usurped the throne and changed the era name to Dechang.

sentences.zh: 己未，軍次幷州。

translations.literal: On jiwei day the army halted at Bing Province.
translations.idiomatic: On jiwei day the army encamped at Bing Province.

sentences.zh: 庚申，延宗擁兵四萬出城抗拒，帝率諸軍合戰，齊人退，帝乘勝逐北，率千餘騎入東門，詔諸軍繞城置陣。

translations.literal: On gengshen day Yanzong led forty thousand troops out of the city to resist; the Emperor led the various armies to join battle; the Qi men retreated; the Emperor pressed the victory in pursuit, leading more than a thousand horsemen into the eastern gate, and ordered the armies to deploy formations around the city.
translations.idiomatic: On gengshen day Yanzong led forty thousand men out to resist. Emperor Wu led the combined armies into battle; the Qi forces fell back, and he pressed the pursuit with more than a thousand horsemen through the eastern gate, then ordered the armies to encircle the city.

sentences.zh: 至夜，延宗率其衆排陣而前，城中軍卻，人相蹂踐，大為延宗所敗，死傷略盡。

translations.literal: By night Yanzong led his masses in battle formation forward; the army in the city fell back; men trampled one another; they were greatly defeated by Yanzong; dead and wounded were nearly all.
translations.idiomatic: That night Yanzong advanced in battle order. The troops inside the city gave way in confusion and trampled one another; Yanzong routed them utterly, and casualties were nearly total.

sentences.zh: 齊人欲閉門，以閽下積尸，扉不得闔。

translations.literal: The Qi men wished to shut the gate, but corpses piled beneath the gate leaves and the doors could not be closed.
translations.idiomatic: The Qi tried to shut the gates, but corpses heaped beneath them and the doors would not close.

sentences.zh: 帝從數騎，崎嶇危險，僅得出門。

translations.literal: The Emperor, with a few horsemen, over perilous ground, barely got out the gate.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu escaped with only a few riders over broken ground and barely got out the gate.

sentences.zh: 至明，率諸軍更戰，大破之，擒延宗，幷州平。

translations.literal: At dawn he led the various armies to fight again, greatly defeated them, captured Yanzong, and Bing Province was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn he led the armies back into battle, routed them completely, captured Yanzong, and pacified Bing Province.

sentences.zh: 壬戌，詔曰：

translations.literal: On renxu day an edict said:
translations.idiomatic: On renxu day an edict declared:

sentences.zh: 昔天厭水運，龍戰於野，兩京圮隔，四紀于茲。

translations.literal: Formerly heaven grew weary of the water dynasty; dragons battled in the wilds; the two capitals were sundered; four reigns have passed since.
translations.idiomatic: Long ago heaven wearied of the water dynasty; dragons battled in the fields; the two capitals stood divided, and four reigns have passed since.

sentences.zh: 朕垂拱巖廊，君臨宇縣，相邠民於海內，混楚弓於天下，一物失所，有若推溝。

translations.literal: I, draped in rule from the cliff gallery, face and govern the realm, harmonizing the people of Bin within the seas and mingling the bows of Chu under heaven—if one thing is lost, it is as though pushed into a ditch.
translations.idiomatic: I have ruled from the court, governing the realm, uniting the people within the seas and bringing all under heaven into one fold—when one person suffers loss, it is as if I had cast him into a ditch.

sentences.zh: 方欲德綏未服，義征不譓。

translations.literal: Just now I wish to soothe by virtue those not yet submitted, and by righteousness campaign against the unyielding.
translations.idiomatic: I mean to win over the unsubmissive by virtue and punish the recalcitrant by righteous force.

sentences.zh: 偽主高緯，放命燕齊，怠慢典刑，俶擾天紀，加以背惠怒鄰，棄信忘義。

translations.literal: The false ruler Gao Wei, reckless in Yan and Qi, negligent of canonical punishments, first disturbing heaven's order, moreover turning his back on kindness and raging at neighbors, abandoning faith and forgetting righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: The usurper Gao Wei ran wild in Yan and Qi, neglected law and punishment, and disturbed the order of heaven; he repaid kindness with enmity, broke faith, and forgot righteousness.

sentences.zh: 朕應天從物，伐罪弔民，一鼓而蕩平陽，再舉而摧勍敵。

translations.literal: I responded to heaven and followed the people, campaigned against crime and consoled the people; one drum-stroke cleared Pingyang; a second thrust shattered the fierce foe.
translations.idiomatic: Answering heaven and following the people, I marched to punish crime and succor the people: one blow cleared Pingyang; a second shattered the enemy.

sentences.zh: 偽署王公，相繼道左。

translations.literal: False-appointed kings and dukes surrendered in succession along the road.
translations.idiomatic: The usurpers' kings and dukes surrendered one after another along the road.

sentences.zh: 高緯智窮數屈，逃竄草間。

translations.literal: Gao Wei's stratagems exhausted and his fate ran out; he fled and hid among the grass.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Wei, his wits spent and his luck gone, fled and hid in the wild.

sentences.zh: 偽安德王高延宗擾攘之間，遂竊名號，與偽齊昌王莫多婁敬顯等，收合餘燼，背城抗敵。

translations.literal: The false Prince of Ande, Gao Yanzong, amid the turmoil stole a title; with the false Prince of Qichang, Mo Duolou Jingxian, and others he gathered the remaining embers, backed the city, and resisted the foe.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Yanzong, the usurping Prince of Ande, seized a title amid the chaos; with Mo Duolou Jingxian, the usurping Prince of Qichang, and others he rallied the remnants and resisted from behind the walls.

sentences.zh: 王威旣振，魚潰鳥離，破竹更難，建瓴非易，延宗衆散，解甲軍門。

translations.literal: Once royal authority was roused, fish scattered and birds fled; splitting bamboo grew harder no more; pouring from a high eave was not easy—Yanzong's masses dispersed and he laid down arms at the army gate.
translations.idiomatic: Once royal authority was raised, the enemy broke like fish in a net and birds from a tree; victory came as easily as splitting bamboo or tipping a jar from a high eave—Yanzong's forces scattered and he surrendered at the camp gate.

sentences.zh: 根本旣傾，枝葉自霣，幽青海岱，折簡而來，冀北河南，傳檄可定。

translations.literal: Once the root was overturned, branches and leaves fell of themselves; from You and Qing to the sea's shore, men came at a written summons; north of Ji and south of the River, a proclamation could settle all.
translations.idiomatic: When the root was gone, the branches fell of themselves; from You and Qing to the eastern sea, men submitted at a summons; north of Ji and south of the Yellow River, a proclamation could settle all.

sentences.zh: 八紘共貫，六合同風，方當偃伯靈台，休牛桃塞，無疆之慶，非獨在余。

translations.literal: The eight cords are threaded as one; the six harmonies share one wind; just now we should rest the troops at the Spirit Terrace and release the oxen at Taosai—the boundless rejoicing is not mine alone.
translations.idiomatic: The realm is united and all share one custom; now we should rest the armies and lay aside the weapons—the boundless rejoicing belongs not to me alone.

sentences.zh: 漢皇約法，除其苛政，姬王輕典，刑彼新邦。

translations.literal: The Han emperor made covenant law and removed harsh government; the Ji king used light statutes and punished the new domain.
translations.idiomatic: The Han emperor made covenant law and abolished harsh rule; the Zhou king applied mild statutes to the newly won lands.

sentences.zh: 思覃惠澤，被之率土，新舊臣民，皆從蕩滌。

translations.literal: Thinking to extend beneficent grace and spread it over the leading soil, new and old subjects and people—all follow full cleansing.
translations.idiomatic: I mean to extend grace across the land; new and old subjects alike shall be cleansed of past guilt.

sentences.zh: 可大赦天下。

translations.literal: A great amnesty may be proclaimed for the empire.
translations.idiomatic: Let a general amnesty be proclaimed throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 高緯及王公以下，若釋然歸順，咸許自新。

translations.literal: Gao Wei and kings and dukes below, if they calmly return in submission, are all permitted self-renewal.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Wei and all kings and officials below him, if they submit peacefully, shall be allowed to start anew.

sentences.zh: 諸亡入偽朝，亦從寬宥。

translations.literal: Those who fled into the false court are also granted broad pardon.
translations.idiomatic: Those who had fled into the usurpers' court shall also receive lenient pardon.

sentences.zh: 官榮次序，依例無失。

translations.literal: Official rank and precedence shall follow precedent without loss.
translations.idiomatic: Official rank and precedence shall be preserved according to precedent.

sentences.zh: 其齊偽制令，卽宜削除。

translations.literal: The false Qi statutes and orders should at once be abolished.
translations.idiomatic: The usurpers' laws and orders shall be abolished at once.

sentences.zh: 鄒魯縉紳，幽幷騎士，一介可稱，並宜銓錄。

translations.literal: Gentry of Zou and Lu, horsemen of You and Bing—if one man is worthy of note, all should be selected and recorded.
translations.idiomatic: Scholars of Zou and Lu, horsemen of You and Bing—any man of merit shall be examined and enrolled.

sentences.zh: 百年去殺，雖或難希，期月有成，庶幾可勉。

translations.literal: A hundred years without capital punishment, though perhaps hard to hope for; accomplishment within a month—one may almost strive for it.
translations.idiomatic: A century without executions may be hard to attain, but results within a month are something we can strive for.

sentences.zh: 丙寅，出齊宮中金銀寶器珠翠麗服及宮女二千人，班賜將士。

translations.literal: On bingyin day gold, silver, precious vessels, pearls, jade, fine robes from the Qi palace, and two thousand palace women were brought out and distributed to officers and soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: On bingyin day gold, silver, jewels, pearls, fine robes from the Qi palace, and two thousand palace women were distributed among the troops.

sentences.zh: 以柱國趙王招、陳王純、越王盛、杞國公亮、梁國公侯莫陳芮、庸國公王謙、北平公寇紹、鄭國公達奚震並為上柱國。

translations.literal: The pillars-of-state, Prince of Zhao Zhao, Prince of Chen Chun, Prince of Yue Sheng, Duke of Qi State Liang, Duke of Liang State Houmochen Rui, Duke of Yong State Wang Qian, Duke of Pingbei Kou Shao, and Duke of Zheng State Daxi Zhen were all made superior pillars-of-state.
translations.idiomatic: Pillars-of-state Yuwen Zhao, Prince of Zhao; Yuwen Chun, Prince of Chen; Yuwen Sheng, Prince of Yue; Liang, Duke of Qi; Houmochen Rui, Duke of Liang; Wang Qian, Duke of Yong; Kou Shao, Duke of Pingbei; and Daxi Zhen, Duke of Zheng were all made superior pillars-of-state.

sentences.zh: 封齊王憲子安城郡公質為河間王，大將軍廣化公丘崇為潞國公，神水公姬願為原國公，廣業公尉遲運為盧國公。

translations.literal: The Prince of Qi State Xian's son, Duke of Ancheng commandery Zhi, was enfeoffed as Prince of Hejian; the grand general, Duke of Guanghua Qiu Chong, as Duke of Lu state; the Duke of Shenshui Ji Yuan as Duke of Yuan state; the Duke of Guangye Yuchi Yun as Duke of Lu state.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi, Duke of Ancheng and son of Yuwen Xian, Prince of Qi, was enfeoffed as Prince of Hejian; Grand General Qiu Chong, Duke of Guanghua, as Duke of Lu; Ji Yuan, Duke of Shenshui, as Duke of Yuan; and Yuchi Yun, Duke of Guangye, as Duke of Lu.

sentences.zh: 諸有功者，封授各有差。

translations.literal: Those with merit received enfeoffments and appointments each according to difference.
translations.idiomatic: Those with merit received enfeoffments and appointments according to their deeds.

sentences.zh: 癸酉，帝率六軍趣鄴。

translations.literal: On guiyou day the Emperor led the Six Armies toward Ye.
translations.idiomatic: On guiyou day Emperor Wu led the Six Armies toward Ye.

sentences.zh: 以上柱國、陳王純為幷州總管。

translations.literal: The superior pillar-of-state, Prince of Chen Chun, was made inspector-general of Bing Province.
translations.idiomatic: Superior Pillar-of-State Yuwen Chun, Prince of Chen, was made inspector-general of Bing Province.

sentences.zh: 六年春正月乙亥，齊主傳位於其太子恆，改年承光，自號為太上皇。

translations.literal: Sixth year, first month of spring, day yihai, the Qi ruler transferred the throne to his crown prince Heng, changed the era name to Chengguang, and styled himself Retired Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Sixth year, first month of spring, on yihai day, the Qi ruler abdicated to his crown prince Heng, changed the era name to Chengguang, and styled himself Retired Emperor.

sentences.zh: 壬辰，帝至鄴。

translations.literal: On renchen day the Emperor reached Ye.
translations.idiomatic: On renchen day Emperor Wu reached Ye.

sentences.zh: 齊主先於城外掘塹豎柵。

translations.literal: The Qi ruler had first dug moats and raised palisades outside the city.
translations.idiomatic: The Qi ruler had already dug trenches and raised palisades outside the city.

sentences.zh: 癸巳，帝率諸軍圍之，齊人拒守，諸軍奮擊，大破之，遂平鄴。

translations.literal: On guisi day the Emperor led the various armies to besiege it; the Qi men defended; the armies struck fiercely and greatly defeated them, then pacified Ye.
translations.idiomatic: On guisi day Emperor Wu besieged the city. The Qi defended stubbornly, but the armies attacked fiercely, routed them, and took Ye.

sentences.zh: 齊主先送其母幷妻子於青州，及城陷，乃率數十騎走青州。

translations.literal: The Qi ruler had first sent his mother, wife, and children to Qing Province; when the city fell he then led several dozen horsemen and fled to Qing Province.
translations.idiomatic: The Qi ruler had already sent his mother, wife, and children to Qing Province; when the city fell he fled there with several dozen horsemen.

sentences.zh: 遣大將軍尉遲勤率二千騎追之。

translations.literal: Grand General Yuchi Qin was dispatched leading two thousand horsemen in pursuit.
translations.idiomatic: Grand General Yuchi Qin was sent in pursuit with two thousand cavalry.

sentences.zh: 是戰也，於陣獲其齊昌王莫多婁敬顯。

translations.literal: In this battle the Prince of Qichang, Mo Duolou Jingxian, was captured in the formation.
translations.idiomatic: In this battle Mo Duolou Jingxian, Prince of Qichang, was captured on the field.

sentences.zh: 帝責之曰：「汝有死罪者三：前從幷走鄴，攜妾棄母，是不孝；

translations.literal: The Emperor reproached him, saying: "You have three crimes deserving death: formerly, fleeing from Bing to Ye, you took concubines and abandoned your mother—this is unfilial;
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu rebuked him: "You deserve death three times over: first, when you fled from Bing to Ye you took concubines and abandoned your mother—that is unfilial;

sentences.zh: 外為偽主戮力，內實通啟於朕，是不忠；

translations.literal: outwardly you exerted force for the false ruler, yet inwardly you secretly opened communications with me—this is disloyal;
translations.idiomatic: outwardly you fought for the usurper, yet inwardly you secretly communicated with me—that is disloyal;

sentences.zh: 送款之後，猶持兩端，是不信。

translations.literal: after submitting your allegiance you still held to both sides—this is faithless.
translations.idiomatic: after submitting you still played both sides—that is faithless.

sentences.zh: 如此用懷，不死何待。

translations.literal: With such intent, if you do not die, what are you waiting for?"
translations.idiomatic: With such a heart, if you are not put to death, what are you waiting for?"

sentences.zh: 」遂斬之。

translations.literal: He was then beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: He was then beheaded.

sentences.zh: 是日，西方有聲如雷者一。

translations.literal: That day, in the west there was one sound like thunder.
translations.idiomatic: That day a thunderclap was heard in the west.

sentences.zh: 甲午，帝入鄴城。

translations.literal: On jiawu day the Emperor entered Ye city.
translations.idiomatic: On jiawu day Emperor Wu entered Ye.

sentences.zh: 齊任城王湝先在冀州，齊主至河，遣其侍中斛律孝卿送傳國璽禪位於湝。

translations.literal: The Prince of Rencheng, Gao Hui, was first at Ji Province; when the Qi ruler reached the river he sent his attendant-in-ordinary Hulu Xiaqing to deliver the imperial seal and transfer the throne to Hui.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Hui, Prince of Rencheng, was then in Ji Province; when the Qi ruler reached the Yellow River he sent Attendant-in-Ordinary Hulu Xiaqing to deliver the imperial seal and abdicate to Hui.

sentences.zh: 孝卿未達，被執送鄴。

translations.literal: Xiaqing did not arrive in time; he was seized and sent to Ye.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaqing did not arrive in time and was captured and sent to Ye.

sentences.zh: 詔去年大赦班宣未及之處，皆從赦例。

translations.literal: An edict ordered that places where last year's great amnesty had not yet been proclaimed should all follow the amnesty precedent.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered that places where last year's general amnesty had not yet been proclaimed should follow the amnesty precedent.

sentences.zh: 封齊開府、洛州刺史獨孤永業為應國公。

translations.literal: The Qi opening-the-feudatory, governor of Luo Province Dugu Yongye, was enfeoffed as Duke of Ying state.
translations.idiomatic: Dugu Yongye, Northern Qi opening-the-feudatory and governor of Luo, was enfeoffed as Duke of Ying.

sentences.zh: 丙申，以上柱國、越王盛為相州總管。

translations.literal: On bingshen day the superior pillar-of-state, Prince of Yue Sheng, was made inspector-general of Xiang Province.
translations.idiomatic: On bingshen day Superior Pillar-of-State Yuwen Sheng, Prince of Yue, was made inspector-general of Xiang Province.

sentences.zh: 己亥，詔曰：「自晉州大陣至于平鄴，身殞戰場者，其子卽授父本官。

translations.literal: On jihai day an edict said: "From the great battle at Jin Province to the pacification of Ye, those whose bodies fell on the battlefield—their sons shall at once receive their fathers' original offices."
translations.idiomatic: On jihai day an edict declared: "From the great battle at Jin Province to the pacification of Ye, the sons of those who fell on the battlefield shall at once receive their fathers' former offices."

sentences.zh: 」尉遲勤擒齊主及其太子恆於青州。

translations.literal: Yuchi Qin captured the Qi ruler and his crown prince Heng at Qing Province.
translations.idiomatic: Yuchi Qin captured the Qi ruler and Crown Prince Heng at Qing Province.

sentences.zh: 庚子，詔曰：「偽齊之末，姦佞擅權，濫罰淫刑，動掛羅網，偽右丞相、咸陽王故斛律明月，偽侍中、特進、開府故崔季舒等七人，或功高獲罪，或直言見誅。
