translations.literal: On gengzi day an edict said: "At the end of false Qi, wicked flatterers monopolized power; punishments were wantonly inflicted and tortures promiscuously applied; nets were cast at every move. The false right chancellor, the late Prince of Xianyang Hulu Mingyue; the false attendant-in-ordinary, specially advanced, opening-the-feudatory, the late Cui Jishu; and seven others—some were punished though their merit was high, some were executed though they spoke straight."
translations.idiomatic: On gengzi day an edict declared: "In the last days of the usurpers' Qi, wicked flatterers held power, punishments were arbitrary, and traps were set at every turn. The late Prince of Xianyang and false right chancellor Hulu Mingyue; the late Attendant-in-Ordinary, specially advanced, and opening-the-feudatory Cui Jishu; and five others—some were punished despite great merit, some were executed for speaking plainly."

sentences.zh: 朕兵以義動，翦除兇暴，表閭封墓，事切下車。

translations.literal: My armies moved by righteousness, cut down the violent and cruel, marked their lanes and sealed their tombs—the matter pressed as upon first descending from the carriage.
translations.idiomatic: My armies marched in the name of righteousness, cut down the violent, and now mark their lanes and seal their tombs—the matter presses as on the day I first entered their land.

sentences.zh: 宜追贈諡，幷窆措。

translations.literal: Posthumous enfeoffments and titles should be conferred, and burial arrangements made together.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumous titles should be conferred and proper burials arranged.

sentences.zh: 其見存子孫，各隨蔭敘錄。

translations.literal: Their surviving sons and grandsons shall each receive inherited appointment and recording according to privilege.
translations.idiomatic: Their surviving sons and grandsons shall receive inherited appointments according to privilege.

sentences.zh: 家口田宅沒官者，並還之。」

translations.literal: Households, fields, and dwellings confiscated by the state shall all be returned."
translations.idiomatic: Households, fields, and dwellings confiscated by the state shall all be restored."

sentences.zh: 辛丑，詔曰：「偽齊叛渙，竊有漳濱，世縱淫風，事窮雕飾。

translations.literal: On xinchou day an edict said: "The false Qi rebelled and scattered, usurping the banks of the Zhang; generation after generation they indulged licentious customs until their affairs reached extreme ornament."
translations.idiomatic: On xinchou day an edict declared: "The usurpers' Qi rebelled and seized the Zhang River lands; generation after generation they indulged debauchery until their extravagance knew no limit."

sentences.zh: 或穿池運石，為山學海；

translations.literal: Some dug pools and moved stone, making mountains to imitate the sea;
translations.idiomatic: Some dug pools and piled stones into mountains to imitate the sea;

sentences.zh: 或層台累構，概日淩雲。

translations.literal: some raised terraces tier on tier, blocking the sun and piercing the clouds.
translations.idiomatic: some built terrace upon terrace, blocking out the sun and piercing the clouds.

sentences.zh: 以暴亂之心，極奢侈之事，有一於此，未或弗亡。

translations.literal: With hearts of violence and disorder they pursued the utmost in luxury—where this existed, none failed to perish.
translations.idiomatic: With violent and disorderly hearts they pursued the utmost luxury—where this existed, ruin followed.

sentences.zh: 朕菲食薄衣，以弘風教，追念生民之費，尚想力役之勞。

translations.literal: I eat sparingly and dress thinly to spread wind and teaching, recalling the cost to the living people, still thinking of the labor of corvée.
translations.idiomatic: I eat plainly and dress simply to set an example, mindful of the cost to the people and the burden of forced labor.

sentences.zh: 方當易茲弊俗，率歸節儉。

translations.literal: Just now we should change these corrupt customs and lead all back to thrift.
translations.idiomatic: Now we must change these corrupt customs and lead all back to thrift.

sentences.zh: 其東山、南園及三臺可並毀撤。

translations.literal: The Eastern Hill, Southern Garden, and Three Terraces may all be demolished together.
translations.idiomatic: The Eastern Hill, Southern Garden, and Three Terraces shall all be demolished.

sentences.zh: 瓦木諸物，凡入用者，盡賜下民。

translations.literal: Tiles, timber, and all other usable materials shall all be bestowed on the common people below.
translations.idiomatic: Tiles, timber, and all usable materials shall be given to the common people.

sentences.zh: 山園之田，各還本主。」

translations.literal: Fields of hill gardens shall each be returned to their original owners."
translations.idiomatic: Garden and hill lands shall be returned to their original owners."

sentences.zh: 二月丙午，論定諸軍功勳，置酒於齊太極殿，會軍士以上，班賜有差。

translations.literal: Second month, day bingwu, military merit of the various armies was assessed and settled; wine was set out in the Qi Grand Harmony Hall; officers and soldiers of rank and above were distributed rewards each according to difference.
translations.idiomatic: Second month, on bingwu day, the armies' merit was assessed; a feast was held in the Qi Grand Harmony Hall for officers and soldiers of rank and above, and rewards were distributed according to merit.

sentences.zh: 丁未，齊主至，帝降自阼階，以賓主之禮相見。

translations.literal: On dingwei day the Qi ruler arrived; the Emperor descended from the throne steps and met him with the rites of host and guest.
translations.idiomatic: On dingwei day the Qi ruler arrived; Emperor Wu descended the throne steps and received him with the rites due a guest.

sentences.zh: 高湝在冀州擁兵未下，遣上柱國、齊王憲與柱國、隨公楊堅率軍討平之。

translations.literal: Gao Hui at Ji Province still held troops and had not submitted; the superior pillar-of-state, Prince of Qi State Xian, and the pillar-of-state, Duke of Sui State Yang Jian, were dispatched leading armies to attack and pacify him.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Hui still held Ji Province with an army; Superior Pillar-of-State Yuwen Xian, Prince of Qi, and Pillar-of-State Yang Jian, Duke of Sui, were sent to subdue him.

sentences.zh: 齊定州刺史、范陽王高紹義叛入突厥。

translations.literal: The Qi governor of Ding Province, the Prince of Fanyang Gao Shaoyi, rebelled and fled into the Turks.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Shaoyi, Qi governor of Ding Province and Prince of Fanyang, rebelled and fled to the Turks.

sentences.zh: 齊諸行臺州鎮悉降，關東平。

translations.literal: All Qi provincial and garrison commands submitted; east of the passes was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: All Qi provincial and garrison commands submitted, and the east was pacified.

sentences.zh: 合州五十五，郡一百六十二，縣三百八十五，戶三百三十萬二千五百二十八，口二千萬六千

translations.literal: In all, fifty-five provinces, one hundred sixty-two commanderies, three hundred eighty-five counties, three million three hundred two thousand five hundred twenty-eight households, and a population of twenty million six thousand
translations.idiomatic: In all there were fifty-five provinces, one hundred sixty-two commanderies, three hundred eighty-five counties, 3,302,528 households, and a population of 20,006,

translations.literal: (six)
translations.idiomatic: (six)

sentences.zh: 百八十六。

translations.literal: hundred eighty-six.

sentences.zh: 乃於河陽、幽、青、南兗、豫、徐、北朔、定並置總管府，相、幷二總管各置宮及六府官。

translations.literal: Then at Heyang, You, Qing, Southern Yan, Yu, Xu, Northern Shuo, and Ding inspector-general headquarters were all established; the Xiang and Bing inspector-generals each had palaces and the six-office staff established.
translations.idiomatic: Inspector-general headquarters were established at Heyang, You, Qing, Southern Yan, Yu, Xu, Northern Shuo, and Ding; the Xiang and Bing commands each received a palace and six-office staff.

sentences.zh: 癸丑，詔曰：「無侮煢獨，事顯前書；

translations.literal: On guichou day an edict said: "Do not insult the solitary and bereft—the matter appears clearly in former books;
translations.idiomatic: On guichou day an edict declared: "Do not wrong the orphaned and alone—the ancients made this plain;

sentences.zh: 哀彼矜人，惠流往訓。

translations.literal: pity those who are to be pitied—beneficence flows from past instruction.
translations.idiomatic: pity those who deserve pity—mercy flows from past instruction.

sentences.zh: 偽齊末政，昏虐寔繁，災甚滔天，毒流比屋。

translations.literal: The last government of false Qi was benighted and cruel in very truth; disaster exceeded flooding heaven; poison flowed house to house.
translations.idiomatic: The usurpers' Qi in its last days was truly benighted and cruel; disaster exceeded the heavens, and poison reached every household.

sentences.zh: 無罪無辜，系虜三軍之手；

translations.literal: Guiltless and innocent, bound in the hands of the three armies;
translations.idiomatic: The innocent were bound in the hands of the armies;

sentences.zh: 不飲不食，僵僕九逵之門。

translations.literal: not drinking, not eating, fallen stiff at the gates of the nine thoroughfares.
translations.idiomatic: without food or drink they collapsed at the city gates.

sentences.zh: 朕為民父母，職養黎人，念甚泣辜，誠深罪己。

translations.literal: I am father and mother to the people; my office is to nurture the black-haired folk; thinking of the weeping innocent, my guilt-feeling is deep and my self-reproach sincere.
translations.idiomatic: I am father and mother to the people and charged with their nurture; thinking of the innocent who weep, my remorse is deep and my self-reproach sincere.

sentences.zh: 除其苛政，事屬改張，宜加寬宥，兼行賑恤。

translations.literal: Removing harsh government belongs to reform and change; lenient pardon should be added, and relief and succor carried out together.
translations.idiomatic: Abolishing harsh rule belongs to reform; lenient pardon and relief should go together.

sentences.zh: 自偽武平三年以來，河南諸州之民，偽齊被掠為奴婢者，不問官私，並宜放免。

translations.literal: From false Wuping year three onward, among the people of the various Henan provinces, those seized by false Qi and made slaves and maidservants—regardless of public or private ownership—all should be released.
translations.idiomatic: From the third year of Wuping onward, among the people of the Henan provinces, all who were seized by the usurpers' Qi and made slaves or maidservants—whether held by officials or private persons—shall be freed.

sentences.zh: 其住在淮南者，亦卽聽還，願

translations.literal: Those living in Huainan may also at once be permitted to return; those who wish
translations.idiomatic: Those living in Huainan may also return at once; those who wish

translations.literal: (to go)
translations.idiomatic: (to go)

sentences.zh: 〔住〕淮北者，可隨便安置。

translations.literal: [to stay] north of the Huai may be settled as convenient.
translations.idiomatic: [to remain] north of the Huai may be settled as they choose.

sentences.zh: 其有癃殘孤老，饑餒絕食，不能自存者，仰刺史守令及親民長司，躬自檢校。

translations.literal: Those who are crippled, aged, orphaned, or starving without food and unable to support themselves—let the provincial governors, magistrates, and local overseers inspect in person.
translations.idiomatic: The crippled, aged, orphaned, and starving who cannot support themselves shall be inspected in person by governors, magistrates, and local overseers.

sentences.zh: 無親屬者，所在給其衣食，務使存濟。」

translations.literal: Those without kin shall be given food and clothing where they are, and every effort made to preserve and succor them."
translations.idiomatic: Those without kin shall be given food and clothing where they are, and every effort made to keep them alive."

sentences.zh: 乙卯，帝自鄴還京。

translations.literal: On yimao day the Emperor returned from Ye to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: On yimao day Emperor Wu returned from Ye to the capital.

sentences.zh: 丙辰，以柱國、隨公楊堅為定州總管。

translations.literal: On bingchen day the pillar-of-state, Duke of Sui State Yang Jian, was made inspector-general of Ding Province.
translations.idiomatic: On bingchen day Pillar-of-State Yang Jian, Duke of Sui, was made inspector-general of Ding Province.

sentences.zh: 三月壬午，詔山東諸州，各舉明經幹治者二人。

translations.literal: Third month, day renwu, an edict ordered the various Shandong provinces each to recommend two men versed in the classics and capable in governance.
translations.idiomatic: Third month, on renwu day, an edict ordered each Shandong province to recommend two men versed in the classics and capable in administration.

sentences.zh: 若奇才異術，卓爾不羣者，弗拘多少。

translations.literal: If there are unusual talents and special skills, outstanding and not of the crowd, do not restrict the number.
translations.idiomatic: Men of unusual talent or special skill, however many, were not to be limited in number.

sentences.zh: 夏四月乙巳，至自東伐。

translations.literal: Summer, fourth month, day yisi, he returned from the eastern campaign.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth month of summer, on yisi day, he returned from the eastern campaign.

sentences.zh: 列齊主於前，其王公等並從，車轝旗幟及器物以次陳於其後。

translations.literal: The Qi ruler was displayed in front; the kings, dukes, and others followed; chariots, banners, flags, and vessels were arrayed in order behind.
translations.idiomatic: The Qi ruler was displayed in front, followed by his kings and dukes; chariots, banners, and captured goods were arrayed behind in order.

sentences.zh: 大駕布六軍，備凱樂，獻俘於太廟。

translations.literal: The imperial carriage deployed the Six Armies, prepared triumphal music, and presented captives at the Imperial Ancestors' Temple.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial procession deployed the Six Armies with triumphal music and presented the captives at the Imperial Ancestors' Temple.

sentences.zh: 京邑觀者皆稱萬歲。

translations.literal: Spectators in the capital all called "Ten thousand years!"
translations.idiomatic: Spectators in the capital all shouted "Long live the emperor!"

sentences.zh: 戊申，封齊主為溫國公。

translations.literal: On wushen day the Qi ruler was enfeoffed as Duke of Wen state.
translations.idiomatic: On wushen day the Qi ruler was enfeoffed as Duke of Wen.

sentences.zh: 庚戌，大會羣臣及諸蕃客於露寢。

translations.literal: On gengxu day a great assembly of ministers and the various frontier guests was held at the Hall of Open Rest.
translations.idiomatic: On gengxu day a great assembly of ministers and foreign envoys was held at the Hall of Open Rest.

sentences.zh: 乙卯，廢蒲、陝、涇、甯四州總管。

translations.literal: On yimao day the inspector-generals of Pu, Shan, Jing, and Ning four provinces were abolished.
translations.idiomatic: On yimao day the inspector-general posts of Pu, Shan, Jing, and Ning provinces were abolished.

sentences.zh: 己巳，祠太廟。

translations.literal: On jisi day sacrifice was offered at the Imperial Ancestors' Temple.
translations.idiomatic: On jisi day he sacrificed at the Imperial Ancestors' Temple.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「東夏旣平，王道初被，齊氏弊政，餘風未殄。

translations.literal: An edict said: "Eastern Xia is already pacified; the royal way is first spread; the corrupt government of the Qi house—its remaining wind is not yet extinguished."
translations.idiomatic: An edict declared: "The east is pacified and the royal way is newly extended, yet the corrupt customs of Qi have not wholly died out."

sentences.zh: 朕劬勞萬機，念存康濟。

translations.literal: I toil at the myriad tasks, thinking always of succor and relief.
translations.idiomatic: I toil at a myriad affairs, ever mindful of the people's welfare.

sentences.zh: 恐清淨之志，未形四海，下民疾苦，不能上達，寢興軫慮，用切於懷。

translations.literal: I fear the will for purity and quiet has not yet taken form within the four seas; the suffering of the people below cannot reach above; lying down and rising, I bend my thoughts—my urgency cuts to the heart.
translations.idiomatic: I fear my wish for clean and simple rule has not yet reached the four seas, and the people's suffering cannot reach me; waking and sleeping, my concern cuts to the heart.

sentences.zh: 宜分遣使人，巡方撫慰，觀風省俗，宣揚治道。

translations.literal: Envoys should be dispatched separately to tour the regions, comfort and reassure, observe customs and inspect the people, and proclaim and spread the way of governance.
translations.idiomatic: Envoys should be sent out to tour the regions, comfort the people, observe local customs, and proclaim the way of governance.

sentences.zh: 有司明立條科，務在弘益。」

translations.literal: The responsible offices should clearly set out statutes and articles, with the task of broad benefit."
translations.idiomatic: The responsible offices should set clear regulations aimed at broad public benefit."

sentences.zh: 五月丁丑，以柱國、譙王儉為大冢宰。

translations.literal: Fifth month, day dingchou, the pillar-of-state, Prince of Qiao Jian, was made grand minister of education.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth month, on dingchou day, Pillar-of-State Yuwen Jian, Prince of Qiao, was made grand minister of education.

sentences.zh: 庚辰，以上柱國杞國公亮為大司徒，鄭國公達奚震為大宗伯，梁國公侯莫陳芮為大司馬，柱國應國公獨孤永業為大司寇，鄖國公韋孝寬為大司空。

translations.literal: On gengchen day the superior pillar-of-state, Duke of Qi State Liang, was made grand minister of the masses; Daxi Zhen, Duke of Zheng state, was made grand director of ceremonies; Houmochen Rui, Duke of Liang state, was made grand marshal; Dugu Yongye, Duke of Ying state and pillar-of-state, was made grand minister of justice; Wei Xiaokuan, Duke of Yun state, was made grand minister of works.
translations.idiomatic: On gengchen day Superior Pillar-of-State Liang, Duke of Qi, was made grand minister of the masses; Daxi Zhen, Duke of Zheng, grand director of ceremonies; Houmochen Rui, Duke of Liang, grand marshal; Dugu Yongye, Duke of Ying and pillar-of-state, grand minister of justice; and Wei Xiaokuan, Duke of Yun, grand minister of works.

sentences.zh: 辛巳，大醮於正武殿，以報功也。

translations.literal: On xinsi day a great jiao rite was held at the Hall of Correct Martiality to report merit.
translations.idiomatic: On xinsi day a great jiao rite was held at the Hall of Correct Martiality to report the victory.

sentences.zh: 己丑，祠方丘。

translations.literal: On jichou day sacrifice was offered at the Square Mound.
translations.idiomatic: On jichou day he sacrificed at the Square Mound.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「朕欽承丕緒，寢興寅畏，惡衣菲食，貴昭儉約。

translations.literal: An edict said: "I reverently receive the great inheritance; lying down and rising I feel reverent awe; I wear poor clothes and eat plain food, honoring thrift and plainness."
translations.idiomatic: An edict declared: "I reverently hold the great inheritance; waking and sleeping I feel awe; I wear plain clothes and eat simple food, honoring thrift."

sentences.zh: 上棟下宇，土階茅屋，猶恐居之者逸，作之者勞，詎可廣廈高堂，肆其嗜欲。

translations.literal: Beams above and foundation below, earthen steps and thatched roofs—still I fear those who dwell there grow idle and those who build grow weary; how can one expand broad halls and high chambers and indulge appetite and desire?
translations.idiomatic: Even earthen steps and thatched roofs make me fear that dwellers grow idle and builders grow weary—how then can one raise broad halls and high chambers to indulge desire?

sentences.zh: 往者，冢臣專任，制度有違，正殿別寢，事窮壯麗。

translations.literal: Formerly the chief minister held sole charge; institutions were at variance; separate main halls and sleeping quarters reached the extreme of splendor and beauty.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly the chief minister held sole power and the regulations went astray; separate main halls and sleeping quarters were built to the utmost splendor.

sentences.zh: 非直雕牆峻宇，深戒前王，而締構弘敞，有踰清廟。

translations.literal: Not only carved walls and towering roofs deeply warn former kings—the structures were grand and broad, exceeding the Clear Temple.
translations.idiomatic: It is not only carved walls and towering roofs that warn former kings—these structures were vast and grand, exceeding even the Clear Temple.

sentences.zh: 不軌不物，何以示後。

translations.literal: What is not according to measure and not according to things—how can it be shown to posterity?
translations.idiomatic: What is out of measure and out of keeping—how can it be shown to posterity?

sentences.zh: 兼東夏初平，民未見德，率先海內，宜自朕始。

translations.literal: Moreover Eastern Xia is newly pacified and the people have not yet seen virtue; to take the lead within the seas, I should begin with myself.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the east is newly pacified and the people have not yet seen virtue; to lead the realm, I must begin with myself.

sentences.zh: 其露寢、會義、崇信、含仁、雲和、思齊諸殿等，農隙之時，悉可毀撤。

translations.literal: The Hall of Open Rest, Hall of Meeting Righteousness, Hall of Honoring Faith, Hall of Embracing Benevolence, Hall of Cloud Harmony, Hall of Shared Thought, and other halls—in the intervals of farming may all be demolished.
translations.idiomatic: The Halls of Open Rest, Meeting Righteousness, Honoring Faith, Embracing Benevolence, Cloud Harmony, and Shared Thought, among others, shall all be demolished in the farming season.

sentences.zh: 雕斲之物，並賜貧民。

translations.literal: Carved objects shall all be bestowed on the poor people.
translations.idiomatic: Carved furnishings shall all be given to the poor.

sentences.zh: 繕造之宜，務從卑樸。

translations.literal: Matters of repair and construction should follow lowliness and plainness."
translations.idiomatic: Any rebuilding shall be plain and modest."

sentences.zh: 」癸巳，行幸雲陽宮。

translations.literal: On guisi day he traveled in state to Yunyang Palace.
translations.idiomatic: On guisi day he traveled to Yunyang Palace.

sentences.zh: 戊戌，詔曰：「京師宮殿，已從撤毀。

translations.literal: On wuxu day an edict said: "The capital's palaces have already been demolished and removed."
translations.idiomatic: On wuxu day an edict declared: "The capital's palaces have already been torn down."

sentences.zh: 並、鄴二所，華侈過度，誠復作之非我，豈容因而弗革。

translations.literal: At Bing and Ye the two sites were excessively lavish and ornate; truly rebuilding them is not my wish—how can I tolerate leaving them unchanged?
translations.idiomatic: At Bing and Ye the palaces were excessively lavish; rebuilding them is not my wish, and I cannot leave them as they are.

sentences.zh: 諸堂殿壯麗，並宜除蕩，甍宇雜物，分賜窮民。

translations.literal: All magnificent halls and chambers should be cleared and swept away; rafters, buildings, and miscellaneous objects shall be divided and bestowed on the destitute people.
translations.idiomatic: All magnificent halls and chambers shall be cleared away; timbers, buildings, and furnishings shall be distributed to the poor.

sentences.zh: 三農之隙，別漸營構，止蔽風雨，務在卑狹。

translations.literal: In the intervals of the three agricultures, construction may gradually proceed by stages, stopping at shelter from wind and rain, with the task in lowliness and narrowness."
translations.idiomatic: In the farming seasons rebuilding may proceed gradually, no more than shelter from wind and rain, and always plain and modest."

sentences.zh: 」庚子，陳遣使來聘。

translations.literal: On gengzi day Chen sent envoys on a friendly mission.
translations.idiomatic: On gengzi day Chen sent envoys on a friendly visit.

sentences.zh: 是月，青城門無故自崩。

translations.literal: That month the Qingyang Gate collapsed for no reason.
translations.idiomatic: That month the Qingyang Gate collapsed without cause.

sentences.zh: 六月丁未，至自雲陽宮。

translations.literal: Sixth month, day dingwei, he returned from Yunyang Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Sixth month, on dingwei day, he returned from Yunyang Palace.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，御正武殿錄囚徒。

translations.literal: On xinhai day he presided at the Hall of Correct Martiality to review prisoners.
translations.idiomatic: On xinhai day he reviewed prisoners at the Hall of Correct Martiality.

sentences.zh: 癸亥，於河州雞鳴防置旭州，甘松防置芳州，廣州防置弘州。

translations.literal: On guihai day at He Province's Jiming garrison Xu Province was established; at Gansong garrison Fang Province was established; at Guangzhou garrison Hong Province was established.
translations.idiomatic: On guihai day Xu Province was established at the Jiming garrison in He Province; Fang Province at the Gansong garrison; and Hong Province at the Guangzhou garrison.

sentences.zh: 甲子，帝東巡。

translations.literal: On jiazi day the Emperor toured east.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi day Emperor Wu toured east.

sentences.zh: 丁卯，詔曰：「同姓百世，婚姻不通，蓋惟重別，周道然也。

translations.literal: On dingmao day an edict said: "Men of the same surname for a hundred generations do not intermarry—this truly honors separation; the way of Zhou was so."
translations.idiomatic: On dingmao day an edict declared: "Men of the same surname do not intermarry for a hundred generations—this honors proper separation; such was the Zhou way."

sentences.zh: 而娶妻買妾，有納母氏之族，雖曰異宗，猶為混雜。

translations.literal: Yet in taking wives and buying concubines some admitted women of the mother's clan; though called a different lineage, it was still mixing and confusion.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in taking wives and buying concubines some admitted women of the maternal clan; though called a different line, it was still improper mixing.

sentences.zh: 自今以後，悉不得娶母同姓，以為〔妻〕妾。

translations.literal: From now onward it is altogether forbidden to take wives of the same surname as one's mother, whether as [wives] or concubines.
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth it is forbidden to take as wife or concubine any woman of the same surname as one's mother.

sentences.zh: 其已定未成者，卽令改聘。」

translations.literal: Those already betrothed but not yet completed shall at once be made to change the engagement."
translations.idiomatic: Betrothals already made but not yet completed shall be broken at once."

sentences.zh: 秋七月己卯，封齊王憲第四子廣都公負為莒國公，紹莒莊公洛生後。

translations.literal: Seventh month of autumn, day jimao, the Prince of Qi State Xian's fourth son, Duke of Guangdu Fu, was enfeoffed as Duke of Ju state, continuing the line of Ju's Duke Zhuang, Luosheng.
translations.idiomatic: Seventh month of autumn, on jimao day, Fu, Duke of Guangdu and fourth son of Yuwen Xian, Prince of Qi, was enfeoffed as Duke of Ju to continue the line of Luosheng, Duke Zhuang of Ju.

sentences.zh: 癸未，應州獻芝草。

translations.literal: On guiwei day Ying Province presented lingzhi fungus.
translations.idiomatic: On guiwei day Ying Province presented lingzhi fungus.

sentences.zh: 丙戌，行幸洛州。

translations.literal: On bingxu day he traveled in state to Luo Province.
translations.idiomatic: On bingxu day he traveled to Luo Province.

sentences.zh: 己丑，詔山東諸州舉有才者，上縣六人，中縣五人，下縣四人，赴行在所，共論治政得失。

translations.literal: On jichou day an edict ordered the various Shandong provinces to recommend men of talent: six from upper counties, five from middle counties, and four from lower counties, to proceed to the imperial camp and together discuss the gains and losses of governance.
translations.idiomatic: On jichou day an edict ordered Shandong provinces to recommend talented men—six from upper counties, five from middle, four from lower—to come to the imperial camp and discuss the merits and failings of government.

sentences.zh: 戊戌，以上柱國、庸公王謙為益州總管。

translations.literal: On wuxu day the superior pillar-of-state, Duke of Yong Wang Qian, was made inspector-general of Yi Province.
translations.idiomatic: On wuxu day Superior Pillar-of-State Wang Qian, Duke of Yong, was made inspector-general of Yi Province.

sentences.zh: 八月壬寅，議定權衡度量，頒於天下。

translations.literal: Eighth month, day renyin, weights and measures were deliberated and fixed, and promulgated throughout the empire.
translations.idiomatic: Eighth month, on renyin day, weights and measures were standardized and promulgated throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 其不依新式者，悉追停。

translations.literal: Those not following the new standard were all ordered to cease.
translations.idiomatic: Those not using the new standard were ordered to stop.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「以刑止刑，世輕世重。

translations.literal: An edict said: "Using punishment to stop punishment—light or heavy by the age."
translations.idiomatic: An edict declared: "Punishment varies in severity from age to age."

sentences.zh: 罪不及嗣，皆有定科。

translations.literal: Guilt not reaching the heirs—all have fixed statutes.
translations.idiomatic: Guilt does not extend to heirs—there are fixed statutes for this.

sentences.zh: 雜役之徒，獨異常憲，一從罪配，百世不免。

translations.literal: Miscellaneous corvée persons alone differ from the regular statutes; once assigned by crime they are never free for a hundred generations.
translations.idiomatic: Miscellaneous corvée households alone stood outside the regular law; once assigned by crime they were never free for generations.

sentences.zh: 罰旣無窮，刑何以措。

translations.literal: When punishment has no end, how can punishment be set aside?
translations.idiomatic: When punishment has no end, how can punishments be abolished?

sentences.zh: 道有沿革，宜從寬典。

translations.literal: The Way has succession and change; lenient statutes should be followed.
translations.idiomatic: The Way changes with the times; lenient statutes should be followed.

sentences.zh: 凡諸雜戶，悉放為民。

translations.literal: All miscellaneous households shall all be released as common people.
translations.idiomatic: All miscellaneous households shall be freed and made common people.

sentences.zh: 配雜之科，因之永削。

translations.literal: The statute of assignment to miscellaneous status is thereby abolished forever."
translations.idiomatic: The law assigning men to miscellaneous status is abolished forever."

sentences.zh: 」甲子，鄭州獻九尾狐，皮肉銷盡，骨體猶具。

translations.literal: On jiazi day Zheng Province presented a nine-tailed fox; flesh and skin had melted away, yet the bones and body remained complete.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi day Zheng Province presented a nine-tailed fox; its flesh and skin had rotted away, but the skeleton remained intact.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「瑞應之來，必昭有德。

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "When auspicious responses come, they surely proclaim virtue."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu said: "When auspicious omens appear, they must proclaim virtue."

sentences.zh: 若使五品時敘，四海和平，家識孝慈，人知禮讓，乃能致此。

translations.literal: If the five ranks are timely ordered, the four seas are at peace, families know filial kindness, and people know ritual yielding—only then can this be brought about.
translations.idiomatic: Only when ranks are properly ordered, the realm is at peace, families know filial piety, and people know courtesy can such things appear.

sentences.zh: 今無其時，恐非實錄。

translations.literal: Now the time is not yet here; I fear this is not a true record."
translations.idiomatic: That time is not yet here; I fear this is no true omen."

sentences.zh: 」乃命焚之。

translations.literal: He then ordered it burned.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered it burned.

sentences.zh: 九月壬申，以柱國鄧國公竇熾、申國公李穆並為上柱國。

translations.literal: Ninth month, day renshen, the pillar-of-state, Duke of Deng Dou Chi, and the pillar-of-state, Duke of Shen Li Mu, were both made superior pillars-of-state.
translations.idiomatic: Ninth month, on renshen day, Pillar-of-State Dou Chi, Duke of Deng, and Pillar-of-State Li Mu, Duke of Shen, were both made superior pillars-of-state.

sentences.zh: 戊寅，初令民庶已上，唯聽衣綢、綿綢、絲布、圓綾、紗、絹、綃、葛、布等九種，餘悉停斷。

translations.literal: On wuyin day it was first ordered that among the people and above, only nine kinds of cloth might be worn: silk, cotton silk, silk cloth, round gauze, gauze, thin silk, fine silk, hemp, and common cloth; all others were stopped and cut off.
translations.idiomatic: On wuyin day it was first ordered that commoners and above might wear only nine kinds of cloth—silk, cotton silk, silk cloth, round gauze, gauze, thin silk, fine silk, hemp, and common cloth; all others were forbidden.

sentences.zh: 朝祭之服，不拘此例。

translations.literal: Court and sacrificial dress was not bound by this rule.
translations.idiomatic: Court and sacrificial dress was exempt from this rule.

sentences.zh: 甲申，絳州獻白雀。

translations.literal: On jiashen day Jiang Province presented a white sparrow.
translations.idiomatic: On jiashen day Jiang Province presented a white sparrow.

sentences.zh: 壬辰，詔東土諸州儒生，明一經已上，並舉送，州郡以禮發遣。

translations.literal: On renchen day an edict ordered Confucian scholars of the eastern provinces who were versed in one classic or more to be recommended and sent; provinces and commanderies were to dispatch them with proper rites.
translations.idiomatic: On renchen day an edict ordered eastern provinces to recommend and send Confucian scholars versed in at least one classic; provinces and commanderies were to dispatch them with proper ceremony.

sentences.zh: 癸卯，封上大將軍、上黃公王軌為郯國公。

translations.literal: On guimao day the grand general, Duke of Shanghuang Wang Gui, was enfeoffed as Duke of Tan state.
translations.idiomatic: On guimao day Grand General Wang Gui, Duke of Shanghuang, was enfeoffed as Duke of Tan.

sentences.zh: 吐谷渾遣使獻方物。

translations.literal: Tuyuhun sent envoys presenting local products.
translations.idiomatic: Tuyuhun sent envoys with tribute.

sentences.zh: 冬十月戊申，行幸鄴宮，戊午，改葬德皇帝於冀州。

translations.literal: Tenth month of winter, day wushen, he traveled in state to Ye Palace; on wuwu day the Virtuous Emperor was reburied at Ji Province.
translations.idiomatic: Tenth month of winter, on wushen day, he traveled to Ye Palace; on wuwu day the Virtuous Emperor was reburied in Ji Province.

sentences.zh: 帝服緦，哭於太極殿，百官素服哭。

translations.literal: The Emperor wore the one-year mourning garment and wept in the Grand Harmony Hall; the hundred offices wept in plain dress.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu wore one-year mourning and wept in the Grand Harmony Hall; the officials wept in plain dress.

sentences.zh: 是月，誅溫國公高緯。

translations.literal: That month Duke of Wen state Gao Wei was executed.
translations.idiomatic: That month Gao Wei, Duke of Wen, was executed.

sentences.zh: 十一月庚午，百濟遣使獻方物。

translations.literal: Eleventh month, day gengwu, Baekje sent envoys presenting local products.
translations.idiomatic: Eleventh month, on gengwu day, Baekje sent envoys with tribute.

sentences.zh: 壬申，封皇子充為道王，兌為蔡王。

translations.literal: On renshen day the imperial son Chong was enfeoffed as Prince of Dao; Dui as Prince of Cai.
translations.idiomatic: On renshen day the imperial son Chong was enfeoffed as Prince of Dao and Dui as Prince of Cai.

sentences.zh: 癸酉，陳將吳明徹侵呂梁，徐州總管梁士彥出軍與戰，不利，退守徐州。

translations.literal: On guiyou day the Chen general Wu Mingche invaded Lüliang; the inspector-general of Xu Province, Liang Shiyan, led troops out to battle, was unsuccessful, and withdrew to defend Xu Province.
translations.idiomatic: On guiyou day the Chen general Wu Mingche invaded Lüliang; Liang Shiyan, inspector-general of Xu Province, gave battle, was defeated, and withdrew to defend Xu.

sentences.zh: 遣上大將軍、郯國公王軌率師討之。

translations.literal: The grand general, Duke of Tan state Wang Gui, was dispatched leading troops to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: Grand General Wang Gui, Duke of Tan, was sent to attack him.

sentences.zh: 是月，稽胡反，遣齊王憲率軍討平之。

translations.literal: That month the Ji-hu rebelled; the Prince of Qi State Xian was dispatched leading troops to attack and pacify them.
translations.idiomatic: That month the Ji-hu rebelled; Yuwen Xian, Prince of Qi, was sent to suppress them.

sentences.zh: 詔自永熙三年七月已來，去年十月已前，東土之民，被抄略在化內為奴婢者；

translations.literal: An edict ordered that from the seventh month of Yongxi year three onward to before the tenth month of last year, among the people of the eastern lands seized and carried off within the transformed realm as slaves and maidservants;
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered that from the seventh month of Yongxi year three through the tenth month of last year, all eastern people seized and enslaved within the realm;

sentences.zh: 及平江陵之後，良人沒為奴婢者：並宜放免。

translations.literal: and after the pacification of Jiangling, common people seized and made slaves and maidservants—all should be released.
translations.idiomatic: and all common people enslaved after the pacification of Jiangling—should be freed.

sentences.zh: 所在附籍，一同民伍。

translations.literal: Where they were, they should be registered and placed in the same commoner companies.
translations.idiomatic: They should be registered where they were and enrolled as commoners.

sentences.zh: 若舊主人猶須共居，聽留為部曲及客女。

translations.literal: If former masters still needed them to dwell together, they were permitted to remain as retainers and guest women.
translations.idiomatic: If former masters still wished them to remain, they might stay on as retainers or serving women.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「正位於中，有聖通典。

translations.literal: An edict said: "Standing in the correct position at the center—there is a sage's penetrating canon."
translations.idiomatic: An edict declared: "Standing in the correct position at the center is the sage's established canon."

sentences.zh: 質文相革，損益不同。

translations.literal: Substance and ornament change each other; increase and decrease differ.
translations.idiomatic: Form and ornament change with the times; rules are adjusted accordingly.

sentences.zh: 五帝則四星之象，三王制六宮之數。

translations.literal: The Five Emperors took the image of the four stars; the Three Kings fixed the number of the six palaces.
translations.idiomatic: The Five Emperors took the image of the four stars; the Three Kings fixed the number of the six palaces.

sentences.zh: 劉、曹已降，等列彌繁，選擇遍於生民，命秩方於庶職。

translations.literal: From Liu and Cao downward the ranks grew ever more numerous; selection spread over the living people; appointments and ranks matched those of common offices.
translations.idiomatic: From the Liu and Cao dynasties onward ranks multiplied; selection spread among the people and palace appointments rivaled ordinary offices.

sentences.zh: 椒房丹地，有衆如雲。

translations.literal: Within the pepper chambers and cinnabar ground, the multitude was like clouds.
translations.idiomatic: Within the inner palace the women were countless as clouds.

sentences.zh: 本由嗜欲之情，非關風化之義。

translations.literal: This arose from appetite and desire—not from the meaning of transforming customs.
translations.idiomatic: This arose from appetite and desire, not from the purpose of moral transformation.

sentences.zh: 朕運當澆季，思復古始，無容廣集子女，屯聚宮掖。

translations.literal: My fate meets a decadent age; I think to restore antiquity's beginning; I cannot broadly gather sons and daughters and mass them in the palace quarters.
translations.idiomatic: My age is a decadent one; I mean to restore the ways of antiquity; I cannot gather hosts of women into the palace.

sentences.zh: 弘贊後庭，事從約簡。

translations.literal: Expanding and honoring the rear court—the affair follows simplicity.
translations.idiomatic: The rear court shall be kept simple.

sentences.zh: 可置妃二人，世婦三人，御妻三人，自茲以外，悉宜減省。」

translations.literal: Two consorts may be established, three world-wives, three chief wives; from this outward all should be reduced and cut."
translations.idiomatic: There may be two consorts, three world-wives, and three chief wives; beyond this all ranks shall be reduced."

sentences.zh: 己亥晦，日有蝕之。

translations.literal: On jihai day, the last day of the month, the sun was eclipsed.
translations.idiomatic: On jihai day, the last day of the month, the sun was eclipsed.

sentences.zh: 初行《刑書要制》。

translations.literal: The Essentials of Punishment in Writing was first implemented.
translations.idiomatic: The Essentials of Punishment in Writing was first promulgated.

sentences.zh: 持杖羣強盜一匹以上，不持杖羣強盜五匹以上，監臨主掌自盜二十匹以上，小盜及詐偽請官物三十匹以上，正長隱五戶及十丁以上、隱地三頃以上者，至死。

translations.literal: Armed bandits in groups stealing one horse or more; unarmed bandits in groups stealing five horses or more; supervising officials in charge stealing twenty horses or more themselves; petty theft and fraudulently requesting official goods of thirty horses or more; headmen concealing five households and ten adult males or more, or concealing land of three qing or more—to death.
translations.idiomatic: Armed bandits stealing one horse or more; unarmed bandits in groups stealing five horses or more; supervising officials stealing twenty horses or more; petty theft or fraudulently claiming thirty horses or more of official goods; headmen concealing five households and ten adult males or more, or three qing of land or more—all punishable by death.

sentences.zh: 《刑書》所不載者，自依律科。

translations.literal: What the Punishment Writing does not record shall each follow the code statutes.
translations.idiomatic: Matters not covered by the Punishment Writing shall follow the regular code.

sentences.zh: 十二月戊午，吐谷渾遣使獻方物。

translations.literal: Twelfth month, day wuwu, Tuyuhun sent envoys presenting local products.
translations.idiomatic: Twelfth month, on wuwu day, Tuyuhun sent envoys with tribute.

sentences.zh: 己未，東壽陽土人反，率衆五千襲幷州城，刺史東平公宇文神舉破平之。

translations.literal: On jiwei day the people of Dongshouyang rebelled, leading five thousand men to raid Bing Province city; the provincial governor, Duke of Dongping Yuwen Shenju, defeated and pacified them.
translations.idiomatic: On jiwei day the people of Dongshouyang rebelled with five thousand men and attacked Bing; Yuwen Shenju, Duke of Dongping and provincial governor, defeated and pacified them.

sentences.zh: 庚申，行幸幷州宮。

translations.literal: On gengshen day he traveled in state to Bing Palace.
translations.idiomatic: On gengshen day he traveled to the Bing Palace.

sentences.zh: 移幷州軍人四萬戶於關中。

translations.literal: Forty thousand households of Bing Province soldiers were moved to Guanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Forty thousand households of Bing Province troops were relocated to Guanzhong.

sentences.zh: 丙寅，以柱國、滕王逌為河陽總管。

translations.literal: On bingyin day the pillar-of-state, Prince of Teng You, was made inspector-general of Heyang.
translations.idiomatic: On bingyin day Pillar-of-State Yuwen You, Prince of Teng, was made inspector-general of Heyang.

sentences.zh: 丁卯，以柱國、隨國公楊堅為南兗州總管，上柱國、申國公李穆為幷州總管。

translations.literal: On dingmao day the pillar-of-state, Duke of Sui State Yang Jian, was made inspector-general of Southern Yan Province; the superior pillar-of-state, Duke of Shen Li Mu, was made inspector-general of Bing Province.
translations.idiomatic: On dingmao day Pillar-of-State Yang Jian, Duke of Sui, was made inspector-general of Southern Yan; Superior Pillar-of-State Li Mu, Duke of Shen, was made inspector-general of Bing.

sentences.zh: 戊辰，廢幷州宮及六府。

translations.literal: On wuchen day the Bing Palace and six offices were abolished.
translations.idiomatic: On wuchen day the Bing Palace and six offices were abolished.

sentences.zh: 是月，北營州刺史高寶甯據州反。

translations.literal: That month the governor of Northern Ying Province, Gao Baoning, held the province and rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: That month Gao Baoning, governor of Northern Ying Province, seized the province and rebelled.

sentences.zh: 三月戊辰，於蒲州置宮。

translations.literal: Third month, day wuchen, a palace was established at Pu Province.
translations.idiomatic: Third month, on wuchen day, a palace was established at Pu Province.

sentences.zh: 廢同州及長春二宮。

translations.literal: Tong Province and the two Changchun palaces were abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Tong Province and the two Changchun palaces were abolished.

sentences.zh: 壬申，突厥遣使獻方物。

translations.literal: On renshen day, the Turks sent envoys presenting local products.
translations.idiomatic: On renshen day Turkish envoys presented tribute goods.

sentences.zh: 甲戌，初服常冠。

translations.literal: On jiaxu day, he first wore the regular cap.
translations.idiomatic: On jiaxu day he first wore the regular cap.

sentences.zh: 以皁紗為之，加簪而不施纓導，其制若今之折角巾也。

translations.literal: It was made of black gauze, with a hairpin added but without tassel or cord; its form was like today's folded-corner kerchief.
translations.idiomatic: It was made of black gauze, pinned but without tassel or cord, and resembled the folded-corner kerchief of the day.

sentences.zh: 上大將軍、郯國公王軌破陳師于呂梁，擒其將吳明徹等，俘斬三萬餘人。

translations.literal: Grand General Wang Gui, Duke of Tan, defeated Chen forces at Lüliang, captured the generals Wu Mingche and others, and killed or captured more than thirty thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: Grand General Wang Gui, Duke of Tan, routed Chen forces at Lüliang, captured Wu Mingche and other commanders, and killed or took more than thirty thousand men.

sentences.zh: 丁亥，詔：「柱國故豆盧寧征江南武陵、南平等郡，所有民庶為人奴婢者，悉依江陵放免。

translations.literal: On dinghai day, an edict said: "The former pillar-of-state Dou Lu Ning, on his campaign in Jiangnan against Wuling and Nanping commanderies, [held] all common people and households as men's and women's slaves; all are to be released according to the Jiangling precedent.
translations.idiomatic: On dinghai day an edict declared: "The late Pillar-of-State Dou Lu Ning, on his Jiangnan campaign against Wuling and Nanping, had taken common people as slaves; all such persons are to be freed according to the Jiangling precedent.

sentences.zh: 」壬辰，改元。

translations.literal: " On renchen day, the era name was changed.
translations.idiomatic: " On renchen day the era name was changed.

sentences.zh: 夏四月壬子，初令遭父母喪者，聽終制。

translations.literal: Summer, fourth month, on renzi day, it was first ordered that those who had suffered the death of parents might observe the full mourning period.
translations.idiomatic: Summer, fourth month, on renzi day, it was first ordered that those mourning parents might complete the full mourning period.

sentences.zh: 庚申，突厥入寇幽州，殺掠吏民。

translations.literal: On gengshen day, the Turks invaded You Province, killing and plundering officials and people.
translations.idiomatic: On gengshen day the Turks raided You Province, killing and plundering officials and commoners.

sentences.zh: 議將討之。

translations.literal: A campaign against them was planned.
translations.idiomatic: Plans were made to campaign against them.

sentences.zh: 五月己丑，帝總戎北伐。

translations.literal: Fifth month, on jichou day, the emperor personally took command of a northern expedition.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth month, on jichou day, the emperor personally led a northern campaign.

sentences.zh: 遣柱國原公姬願、東平公宇文神舉等率軍，五道俱入。

translations.literal: Pillar-of-State Ji Yuan, Duke of Yuan, and Eastern Peace Duke Yuwen Shenju and others were dispatched to lead armies; all five routes entered together.
translations.idiomatic: Pillar-of-State Ji Yuan, Duke of Yuan, Eastern Peace Duke Yuwen Shenju, and others were sent with armies on five routes at once.

sentences.zh: 發關中公私驢馬，悉從軍。

translations.literal: Public and private donkeys and horses throughout Guanzhong were requisitioned; all went with the army.
translations.idiomatic: Every public and private donkey and horse in Guanzhong was requisitioned for the campaign.

sentences.zh: 癸巳，帝不豫，止于雲陽宮。

translations.literal: On guisi day, the emperor fell ill and stopped at Yunyang Palace.
translations.idiomatic: On guisi day the emperor fell ill and halted at Yunyang Palace.

sentences.zh: 丙申，詔停諸軍事。

translations.literal: On bingshen day, an edict halted all military operations.
translations.idiomatic: On bingshen day an edict halted all military operations.

sentences.zh: 六月丁酉，帝疾甚，還京。

translations.literal: Sixth month, on dingyou day, the emperor's illness was extreme; he returned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Sixth month, on dingyou day, the emperor grew gravely ill and returned to the capital.

sentences.zh: 其夜，崩於乘輿。

translations.literal: That night he died in his carriage.
translations.idiomatic: That night he died in his carriage.

sentences.zh: 時年三十六。

translations.literal: He was then thirty-six years old.
translations.idiomatic: He was thirty-six years old.

sentences.zh: 遺詔曰：

translations.literal: His final testament said:
translations.idiomatic: His final testament said:

sentences.zh: 人肖形天地，稟質五常，修短之期，莫非命也。

translations.literal: Human beings take form from heaven and earth, receive their substance from the five constants, and the span of life long or short is all fate.
translations.idiomatic: Human beings take shape from heaven and earth and receive their nature from the five constants; whether life is long or short is all a matter of fate.

sentences.zh: 朕君臨宇縣，十有九年，未能使百姓安樂，刑措罔用，所以昧旦求衣，分宵忘寢。

translations.literal: I have ruled the realm for nineteen years, yet have been unable to give the people ease and joy or bring punishments to rest unused; therefore I seek clothing before dawn and forget sleep by dividing the night.
translations.idiomatic: I have ruled the realm for nineteen years, yet have not made the people secure and content or brought punishments to disuse; therefore I rise before dawn and divide the night without sleep.

sentences.zh: 昔魏室將季，海內分崩，太祖扶危翼傾，肇開王業。

translations.literal: In former days when the Wei house was nearing its end, the realm split apart within the seas; the Grand Progenitor supported the tottering and winged the falling, and thereby opened the royal enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: In former days, as the Wei house neared its end and the realm split apart, the Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai steadied the tottering and opened the royal enterprise.

sentences.zh: 燕趙榛蕪，久竊名號。

translations.literal: Yan and Zhao lay waste and overgrown; for long they usurped titles and designations.
translations.idiomatic: Yan and Zhao lay waste and overgrown; for long they usurped titles and regalia.

sentences.zh: 朕上述先志，下順民心，遂與王公將帥，共平東夏。

translations.literal: I, above, carried forward the former resolve and, below, followed the people's hearts; thereupon, with kings, dukes, commanders, and generals, together pacified the Eastern Xia.
translations.idiomatic: Above I carried forward the former resolve; below I followed the people's hearts; and with kings, dukes, and generals together I pacified the Eastern Xia.

sentences.zh: 雖復妖氛蕩定，而民勞未康。

translations.literal: Though demonic vapors were swept clear, the people's toil was not yet at ease.
translations.idiomatic: Though the evil tide was swept away, the people's labor was not yet eased.

sentences.zh: 每一念此，如臨冰谷。

translations.literal: Every time I think of this, it is as though standing beside an icy ravine.
translations.idiomatic: Every time I think of this, it is as though standing on the edge of an icy chasm.

sentences.zh: 將欲包舉六合，混同文軌。

translations.literal: I meant to encompass the six directions and unify culture and the cart-tracks.
translations.idiomatic: I meant to take in all under heaven and unify culture and the imperial roads.

sentences.zh: 今遘疾大漸，氣力稍微，有志不申，以此歎息。

translations.literal: Now I have encountered serious illness; my strength is slightly diminished; my resolve cannot be fulfilled—therefore I sigh at this.
translations.idiomatic: Now my illness has grown grave and my strength has waned; my resolve cannot be fulfilled—and so I sigh.

sentences.zh: 天下事重，萬機不易。

translations.literal: The affairs of the realm are weighty; the myriad duties of state are not easy.
translations.idiomatic: The affairs of the realm are weighty; the myriad duties of state are not easily managed.

sentences.zh: 王公以下，爰及庶僚，宜輔導太子，副朕遺意。

translations.literal: From kings and dukes down to the common clerks, you should assist and guide the crown prince according to my testament's intent.
translations.idiomatic: From kings and dukes down to common officials, you should assist and guide the crown prince according to my testament's intent.

sentences.zh: 令上不負太祖，下無失為臣。

translations.literal: Make it so that above we do not fail the Grand Progenitor and below we do not fail as ministers.
translations.idiomatic: See to it that above you do not fail the Grand Progenitor and below you do not fail as ministers.

sentences.zh: 朕雖瞑目九泉，無所復恨。

translations.literal: Though my eyes close in the nine springs, I shall have nothing further to regret.
translations.idiomatic: Though my eyes close in the grave, I shall have nothing left to regret.

sentences.zh: 朕平生居處，每存菲薄，非直以訓子孫，亦乃本心所好。

translations.literal: In my lifetime my dwelling has always been kept frugal—not merely to instruct my sons and grandsons, but because it is what my heart itself loves.
translations.idiomatic: In life I have always kept my dwelling frugal—not only to instruct my sons and grandsons, but because my heart itself loves it.

sentences.zh: 喪事資用，須使儉而合禮，墓而不墳，自古通典。

translations.literal: The resources for funeral rites must be kept economical yet conform to ritual; tomb without mound is the common rule since antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: Funeral expenses must be economical yet conform to ritual; burial without a mound is the ancient common rule.

sentences.zh: 隨吉卽葬，葬訖公除。

translations.literal: Follow the auspicious day and bury immediately; when burial is complete, public mourning ends.
translations.idiomatic: Follow the auspicious day and bury at once; when burial is complete, public mourning ends.

sentences.zh: 四方士庶，各三日哭。

translations.literal: Gentlemen and commoners everywhere shall weep for three days each.
translations.idiomatic: Gentry and commoners everywhere shall mourn for three days each.

sentences.zh: 妃嬪以下無子者，悉放還家。

translations.literal: Consorts and concubines below who have no sons shall all be sent back home.
translations.idiomatic: Consorts and concubines without sons shall all be sent home.

sentences.zh: 諡曰武皇帝，廟稱高祖。

translations.literal: His posthumous title was Emperor Wu; his temple name was High Ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: His posthumous title was Emperor Wu; his temple name was High Ancestor.

sentences.zh: 己未，葬於孝陵。

translations.literal: On jiwei day, he was buried at Xiaoling.
translations.idiomatic: On jiwei day he was buried at Xiaoling.

sentences.zh: 帝沉毅有智謀。

translations.literal: The emperor was deep, resolute, and possessed of wisdom and design.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was deep, resolute, and possessed of wisdom and design.

sentences.zh: 初以晉公護專權，常自晦跡，人莫測其深淺。

translations.literal: At first, because Duke of Jin Yuwen Hu monopolized power, he often kept his own track hidden; no one could fathom his depth or shallowness.
translations.idiomatic: At first, because Duke of Jin Yuwen Hu monopolized power, he often kept himself concealed and no one could fathom his depth.

sentences.zh: 及誅護之後，始親萬機。

translations.literal: Only after Hu was executed did he personally attend to the myriad affairs of state.
translations.idiomatic: Only after Hu was executed did he personally attend to the myriad affairs of state.

sentences.zh: 克己勵精，聽覽不怠。

translations.literal: He restrained himself and strove diligently; he heard and reviewed affairs without slackening.
translations.idiomatic: He restrained himself and strove diligently, hearing and reviewing affairs without slackening.

sentences.zh: 用法嚴整，多所罪殺。

translations.literal: He applied the law strictly and justly, and many were condemned to death.
translations.idiomatic: He applied the law strictly and many were condemned to death.

sentences.zh: 號令懇惻，唯屬意於政。

translations.literal: His orders and commands were earnest and tender; he set his mind solely on government.
translations.idiomatic: His orders were earnest and tender, and he set his mind solely on government.

sentences.zh: 羣下畏服，莫不肅然。

translations.literal: His subordinates stood in awe of him; none failed to be reverent.
translations.idiomatic: His subordinates stood in awe of him; none failed to be reverent.

sentences.zh: 性旣明察，少於恩惠。

translations.literal: By nature he was perceptive and discerning, and showed little favor and grace.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was perceptive and discerning, and showed little favor and grace.

sentences.zh: 凡布懷立行，皆欲踰越古人。

translations.literal: In every manner of broad intent and established conduct, he wished to surpass the men of old.
translations.idiomatic: In every broad intent and established conduct, he wished to surpass the men of old.

sentences.zh: 身衣布袍，寢布被，無金寶之飾，諸宮殿華綺者，皆撤毀之，改為土階數尺，不施櫨栱。

translations.literal: He wore hemp robes himself, slept under hemp quilts, and used no gold or gems for adornment; all palace halls that were flowery and fine he had dismantled and destroyed, changing them to earthen platforms several feet high without bracket sets.
translations.idiomatic: He wore hemp robes and slept under hemp quilts, with no gold or gem adornment; flowery palace halls he had dismantled and replaced with earthen platforms several feet high, without bracket sets.

sentences.zh: 其雕文刻鏤，錦繡纂組，一皆禁斷。

translations.literal: Carved patterns and inlay, brocade and embroidery and fine weaving—all were forbidden and cut off.
translations.idiomatic: Carved ornament, brocade, embroidery, and fine weaving—all were forbidden.

sentences.zh: 後宮嬪禦，不過十餘人。

translations.literal: Consorts and concubines in the rear palace did not exceed a dozen or so.
translations.idiomatic: Consorts and concubines in the rear palace numbered no more than a dozen or so.

sentences.zh: 勞謙接下，自強不息。

translations.literal: He toiled humbly in receiving subordinates and strove without ceasing.
translations.idiomatic: He toiled humbly in receiving subordinates and strove without ceasing.

sentences.zh: 以海內未康，銳情教習。

translations.literal: Because the realm within the seas was not yet at peace, he sharpened his resolve to teach and train.
translations.idiomatic: Because the realm was not yet at peace, he sharpened his resolve to teach and train.

sentences.zh: 至於校兵閱武，步行山谷，履涉勤苦，皆人所不堪。

translations.literal: When it came to drilling soldiers and reviewing martial affairs, walking mountain valleys and treading through toil and hardship—all were what others could not endure.
translations.idiomatic: When drilling soldiers and reviewing martial affairs, walking mountain valleys and enduring hardship—all were what others could not bear.

sentences.zh: 平齊之役，見軍士有跣行者，帝親脫靴以賜之。

translations.literal: During the campaign to pacify Qi, seeing a soldier walking barefoot, the emperor personally removed his boots to give them.
translations.idiomatic: During the campaign to pacify Qi, seeing a soldier walking barefoot, the emperor took off his own boots and gave them to him.

sentences.zh: 每宴會將士，必自執杯勸酒，或手付賜物。

translations.literal: Whenever he feasted with commanders and soldiers, he would himself hold the cup to urge wine, or personally hand out gifts.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he feasted with commanders and soldiers, he himself held the cup to urge them to drink, or personally handed out gifts.

sentences.zh: 至於征伐之處，躬在行陣。

translations.literal: When it came to places of campaign, he was personally in the battle line.
translations.idiomatic: On campaign he was personally in the battle line.

sentences.zh: 性又果決，能斷大事。

translations.literal: By nature he was also resolute and decisive, able to decide great matters.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was also resolute and decisive, able to decide great matters.

sentences.zh: 故能得士卒死力，以弱制強。

translations.literal: Therefore he could obtain the soldiers' utmost effort and use weakness to overcome strength.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore he could win the soldiers' utmost effort and use weakness to overcome strength.

sentences.zh: 破齊之後，遂欲窮兵極武，平突厥，定江南，一二年間，必使天下一統，此其志也。

translations.literal: After breaking Qi, he then wished to exhaust the army to the utmost in war, pacify the Turks, and settle Jiangnan; within a year or two he would surely unify the realm under heaven—this was his resolve.
translations.idiomatic: After breaking Qi, he wished to press war to the limit, pacify the Turks, and settle Jiangnan; within a year or two he would unify the realm—this was his resolve.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：自東西否隔，二國爭強，戎馬生郊，干戈日用，兵連禍結，力敵勢均，疆埸之事，一彼一此。

translations.literal: The historian writes: Since east and west were sundered and two states contended in strength, war-horses were born in the suburbs and weapons were used daily; armies connected and calamities bound together; strength matched and momentum was equal; on the borders affairs alternated now this side, now that.
translations.idiomatic: The historian writes: With east and west sundered and two states contending, war-horses foaled in the suburbs and weapons saw daily use; armies linked and calamities compounded; strength and momentum were evenly matched, and border affairs shifted back and forth.

sentences.zh: 高祖纘業，未親萬機，慮遠謀深，以蒙養正。

translations.literal: High Ancestor Yuwen Yong continued the enterprise but had not yet personally attended to the myriad duties; he planned far and thought deeply, nourishing correctness through concealment.
translations.idiomatic: High Ancestor Yuwen Yong continued the enterprise before yet attending to the myriad duties; he planned far and thought deeply, concealing himself to cultivate the right way.

sentences.zh: 及英威電發，朝政惟新，內難旣除，外略方始。

translations.literal: When his heroic might flashed like lightning, court governance was renewed; internal troubles were removed and external strategy began.
translations.idiomatic: When his heroic might flashed like lightning, court governance was renewed; internal troubles were removed and external strategy began.

sentences.zh: 乃苦心焦思，克己勵精，勞役為士卒之先，居處同匹夫之儉。

translations.literal: Thereupon he wore his heart and burned his thoughts, restrained himself and strove diligently, taking toil as the soldiers' forerunner and dwelling as frugally as a common man.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he wore his heart thin and burned his thoughts, restrained himself and strove diligently, taking hardship before his soldiers and dwelling as frugally as a common man.

sentences.zh: 脩富民之政，務強兵之術，乘讐人之有釁，順大道而推亡。

translations.literal: He cultivated policies to enrich the people and devoted himself to methods to strengthen the army; riding the enemy's opening and following the Great Way to overthrow the doomed.
translations.idiomatic: He cultivated policies to enrich the people and devoted himself to strengthening the army; seizing the enemy's opening, he followed the Great Way to overthrow the doomed.

sentences.zh: 五年之間，大勳斯集。

translations.literal: Within five years, great merit was gathered together.
translations.idiomatic: Within five years, great merit was gathered together.

sentences.zh: 攄祖宗之宿憤，拯東夏之阽危，盛矣哉，其有成功者也。

translations.literal: He unleashed the longstanding wrath of the imperial ancestors and rescued the Eastern Xia from imminent peril—splendid indeed! There was merit that succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: He unleashed the imperial ancestors' longstanding wrath and rescued the Eastern Xia from imminent peril—splendid indeed! Here was success.

sentences.zh: 若使翌日之瘳無爽，經營之志獲申，黷武窮兵，雖見譏於良史，雄圖遠略，足方駕於前王者歟。

translations.literal: Had recovery on the morrow been without error and his plans of governance been fulfilled, exhausting martial force and pressing armies to the limit—though reproached by worthy historians—the heroic design and far-reaching strategy would suffice to stand level with former kings, would they not?
translations.idiomatic: Had his recovery on the morrow been assured and his governing plans fulfilled, exhausting martial force and pressing armies to the limit—though reproached by worthy historians—his heroic design and far-reaching strategy would suffice to stand level with former kings, would they not?

sentences.zh: 全文以中華書局、一九七一年十一月版《周書》為本校。

translations.literal: The entire text has been collated against the Zhonghua Shuju edition of the Book of Zhou, November 1971.
translations.idiomatic: The entire text has been collated against the Zhonghua Shuju edition of the Book of Zhou, November 1971.
